     1→# Lock Code Manager
     2→
     3→Lock Code Manager is a Home Assistant integration that keeps PIN codes in sync
     4→across one or more locks, even across different lock providers (e.g. Z-Wave and
     5→Matter locks sharing the same codes). Define your codes once and Lock Code
     6→Manager handles setting, clearing, and monitoring them on every lock.
     7→
     8→Features:
     9→
    10→- Synchronize PIN codes across multiple locks and providers
    11→- Automatic sync — codes are set and cleared as needed, with retry and
    12→  drift detection
    13→- Condition entities control when a code is active:
    14→  - `calendar` — active during events
    15→  - `binary_sensor` / `switch` / `input_boolean` — active when on
    16→  - `schedule` — active during scheduled times
    17→- [Blueprints](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Blueprints)
    18→  for usage limiting, calendar-driven PINs, and more
    19→- Dashboard cards for managing codes and viewing lock status
    20→
    21→Locks from the following integrations are currently supported:
    22→
    23→**Core integrations:**
    24→
    25→- [Matter][wiki-matter]
    26→- [Schlage WiFi][wiki-schlage]
    27→- [Z-Wave](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/zwave_js/)
    28→
    29→**Custom integrations:**
    30→
    31→- [Akuvox][wiki-akuvox] (via [Local Akuvox][local-akuvox])
    32→- [Virtual][wiki-virtual] (via [hass-virtual][hass-virtual])
    33→
    34→[wiki-akuvox]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Akuvox-integration
    35→[wiki-matter]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Matter-integration
    36→[wiki-schlage]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Schlage-integration
    37→[wiki-virtual]: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Virtual-integration
    38→[local-akuvox]: https://github.com/pjaudiomv/hass-local-akuvox
    39→[hass-virtual]: https://github.com/twrecked/hass-virtual
    40→
    41→The code was written to make it (I think) easy to add support for locks in other
    42→integrations. Check the [Wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki) if you
    43→want to learn more about that and take a stab at it. Contributors welcome!
    44→
    45→## Integrations That Cannot Currently Be Supported
    46→
    47→Some lock integrations cannot currently be supported due to limitations in their underlying
    48→libraries. See the [wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Unsupported-Integrations)
    49→for details.
    50→
    51→## Condition Entity Integrations Not Supported
    52→
    53→Some condition entity integrations are not compatible. See the
    54→[wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Unsupported-Condition-Entity-Integrations)
    55→for details.
    56→
    57→## Installation
    58→
    59→The best way to install this integration is via HACS.
    60→
    61→1. Set up your locks as entities to your Home Assistant instance through the corresponding
    62→   integration (e.g. Z-Wave)
    63→2. Add this repository as a custom integration repository in HACS
    64→3. Go to Settings > Devices & Services > Add Integration
    65→4. Select Lock Code Manager
    66→5. Follow the prompts - additional information about the configuration options are
    67→   available in the Wiki
    68→
    69→## Blueprints
    70→
    71→Pre-built automations for common patterns:
    72→
    73→- **Slot Usage Limiter** — Disable a slot after a set number of uses
    74→  [![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fslot_usage_limiter.yaml)
    75→- **Calendar PIN Setter** — Extract and set PINs from calendar event attributes
    76→  [![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fcalendar_pin_setter.yaml)
    77→- **Calendar Condition** — Control slot access based on calendar events
    78→  [![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Ftemplate%2Flock_code_manager%2Fcalendar_condition.yaml)
    79→
    80→See the [wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Blueprints) for detailed setup and configuration.
    81→
    82→## Learn More
    83→
    84→Visit the [Wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki) for detailed
    85→documentation including configuration, troubleshooting, dashboard setup, and development guides.
    86→
    87→## UI & Dashboards
    88→
    89→Lock Code Manager provides Lovelace strategies and custom cards for managing PINs.
    90→See the [wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Add-a-UI-for-lock-code-management)
    91→for configuration options and setup guidance.
    92→
    93→## Inspiration
    94→
    95→I spent some time contributing to [keymaster](https://github.com/FutureTense/keymaster),
    96→and what I learned working on it, and the regular complaints users had about it generating
    97→too many automations, entities, etc. led me to take a different approach. This isn't a
    98→knock on `keymaster`, unfortunately a lot of what is built in this integration wasn't
    99→possible for most of `keymaster`'s life. I briefly considered implementing this into
   100→`keymaster` but:
   101→
   102→1. `keymaster` is still a great solution that works as is, and is more feature rich than
   103→   this integration will likely ever be.
   104→2. `keymaster` is surprisingly simple under the hood because it makes Home Assistant do a
   105→   lot of the heavy lifting for figuring out when to enable and disable a usercode. This
   106→   integration, on the other hand, attempts to do all of the heavy lifting internally in
   107→   code, which means it will generate less entities and automations but it is likely more
   108→   fragile to changes in HA Core or even changes in the codebase.
   109→3. It would be impossible to seamlessly migrate users from the current implementation of
   110→   `keymaster` to this integration's implementation. Rewriting `keymaster` to do this
   111→   would have been the equivalent of creating a new integration anyway, and since it's a
   112→   separate integration, users have a choice of what implementation they want to use.
   113→   Additionally, you can install the integrations side by side and slowly migrate your
   114→   locks over in either direction as needed.
   115→
   116→## Thanks
   117→
   118→A big thank you to the other `keymaster` maintainers:
   119→
   120→- @FutureTense
   121→- @firstof9
   122→
   123→As well as the person who created the base concept that `keymaster` evolved from:
   124→@ptdalen
   125→
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager.wiki/Z-Wave-integration.md",
  "content": "# Z-Wave Integration\n\nLock Code Manager supports Z-Wave locks via the [Z-Wave JS](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/zwave_js/) integration in Home Assistant.\n\n## How It Works\n\nZ-Wave locks store PIN codes in numbered user code slots. Lock Code Manager reads, sets, and clears these codes via the Z-Wave JS driver. Most Z-Wave locks support push updates — when a code is used or changed, the lock notifies Home Assistant immediately.\n\nSome Z-Wave locks mask PIN codes (returning `****` instead of the actual value). Lock Code Manager handles this transparently — masked codes are treated as \"occupied but unreadable\" and the configured PIN is shown in the sensor display.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- The [Z-Wave JS](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/zwave_js/) integration configured in Home Assistant\n- A Z-Wave lock with user code support\n\n## Supported Operations\n\n| Operation | Supported | Notes |\n|-----------|-----------|-------|\n| Set PIN | Yes | Via Z-Wave JS `set_lock_usercode` service |\n| Clear PIN | Yes | Via Z-Wave JS `clear_lock_usercode` service |\n| Read PIN | Varies | Some locks return actual PINs, others mask them |\n| Push updates | Yes | Real-time notifications for code changes and usage |\n| Code slot events | Yes | Reports which code was used to unlock |\n\n## Features\n\n- **Push updates**: Code changes and lock operations are reported in real time (no polling delay)\n- **Code slot events**: The `pin_used` event entity fires when a specific code is used, enabling automations like the Slot Usage Limiter blueprint\n- **Duplicate code detection**: Detects when a lock rejects a code because it duplicates an existing one\n- **Drift detection**: Periodically verifies codes on the lock match the configured values\n\n## Limitations\n\n- **Masked PINs**: Some Z-Wave locks (e.g. certain Schlage models via Z-Wave) mask PIN values. Lock Code Manager cannot read the actual PIN back but handles sync correctly.\n- **Lock-specific behavior**: Different Z-Wave lock brands may handle user code slots differently (e.g. slot numbering, status reporting).\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Codes not syncing\n\nCheck that the Z-Wave JS integration is loaded and the lock entity is available. Verify the lock's node is not in a failed state in the Z-Wave JS control panel.\n\n### \"Code rejected\" errors\n\nThe lock rejected the PIN. Common causes: PIN too short/long for the lock, duplicate PIN already on another slot, or the slot is firmware-disabled.\n\n### Masked PINs showing as \"unknown\"\n\nThis is normal for locks that mask their codes. The code sensor shows the configured PIN for display purposes. The sync indicator assumes the code is correct after a successful set.\n"
}
```

   100→possible for most of `keymaster`'s life. I briefly considered implementing this into
   101→`keymaster` but:
   102→
   103→1. `keymaster` is still a great solution that works as is.
   104→2. `keymaster` is surprisingly simple under the hood because it makes Home Assistant do a
   105→   lot of the heavy lifting for figuring out when to enable and disable a usercode. This
   106→   integration, on the other hand, attempts to do all of the heavy lifting internally in
   107→   code, which means it will generate less entities and automations but it is likely more
   108→   fragile to changes in HA Core or even changes in the codebase.
   109→3. It would be impossible to seamlessly migrate users from the current implementation of
   110→   `keymaster` to this integration's implementation. Rewriting `keymaster` to do this
   111→   would have been the equivalent of creating a new integration anyway, and since it's a
   112→   separate integration, users have a choice of what implementation they want to use.
   113→   Additionally, you can install the integrations side by side and slowly migrate your
   114→   locks over in either direction as needed.

    63→
    64→### Convert Config and Internal Dicts to Dataclasses
    65→
    66→Convert config entry data to typed dataclasses with `from_dict`/`from_entry`
    67→class methods. Use object instances internally instead of iterating through raw
    68→config dicts. Audit codebase for other complex dicts that would benefit from
    69→dataclass conversion (e.g., slot data, lock state, coordinator data). This
    70→improves type safety, IDE autocompletion, and code readability.

Current understanding: prefer\n   `options` only within the config entry update listener during options updates;\n   elsewhere use `data` to avoid mid-update inconsistencies.\n\n#### Sync Manager Follow-ups\n\n- Consider coordinator owning sync managers instead of binary sensor entities\n  (manager lifecycle would survive entity recreation during config updates)\n\n### Convert Config and Internal Dicts to Dataclasses\n\nConvert config entry data to typed dataclasses with `from_dict`/`from_entry`\nclass methods. Use object instances internally instead of iterating through raw\nconfig dicts. Audit codebase for other complex dicts that would benefit from\ndataclass conversion (e.g., slot data, lock state, coordinator data). This\nimproves type safety, IDE autocompletion, and code readability.\n\n**Why not Voluptuous?** Voluptuous is for validation, not object instantiation.\nOther options like `dacite` or Pydantic add dependencies.\n\n### Add Optional Flags to `get_config_entry_data` Websocket Command\n\nNot all callers need all the data from `get_config_entry_data`. Add optional\n`include_entities` and `include_locks` flags (default `True` for backwards\ncompatibility) to skip expensive entity registry queries when not needed.\n\n### Entity Registry Change Detection\n\nTrack entity registry updates and warn if LCM entities change entity IDs (reload\nrequired).\n\n### Add Provider Diagnostic Data Method\n\nAdd `get_diagnostic_data()` method to `BaseLock` for exposing provider-specific\ndiagnostic information.\n\n### Drift Detection Failure Alerting\n\nAdd mechanism to alert users when drift detection consistently fails over\nextended periods (e.g., lock offline). Currently failures are logged but there is\nno visibility to users or entities.\n\n## Features\n\n### Add Support for Additional Lock Providers\n\n**Current Providers:**\n\n- Akuvox (`akuvox.py`) - via Local Akuvox custom integration\n- Matter (`matter.py`)\n- Schlage (`schlage.py`)\n- Z-Wave JS (`zwave_js.py`)\n- Virtual (`virtual.py`) - for testing only\n\n**Open PRs:**\n\n- **ZHA** (#739) - Zigbee Home Automation\n- **MQTT/Zigbee2MQTT** (#740) - MQTT-based locks\n\n**Potential Future Providers:**\n\n- **Nuki** - Popular in Europe\n- **SwitchBot** - Growing popularity\n- **SmartThings** - Large user base\n\n**Cannot Be Supported** (see README for details):\n\n- `esphome` - No user code API in ESPHome\n- `august`, `yale`, `yalexs_ble`, `yale_smart_alarm` - Library limitations\n\nSee `AGENTS.md` for implementation approach and `BaseLock` interface.\n\n### Custom Jinja Templates\n\nShip a `.jinja` file with helper macros for LCM entity resolution (e.g.\n`lcm_slot_entities(config_entry_id, slot_num)` to get PIN, name, enabled,\nactive entity IDs without regex matching). HA loads `.jinja` files from\n`config/custom_templates/` at startup and they're used via\n`{% from 'lcm.jinja' import macro_name %}`. LCM could auto-install the\nfile to `custom_templates/` during setup, similar to how it installs\nLovelace resources.\n\n### Improve Dashboard UI/UX\n\n- Bulk operations (enable/disable multiple slots)\n- Import/export slot configuration\n\n### Add Service Actions\n\n- `lock_code_manager.set_temporary_code` - Create time-limited PIN\n- `lock_code_manager.generate_pin` - Auto-generate secure PIN\n- `lock_code_manager.bulk_enable` / `bulk_disable` - Enable/disable multiple slots\n- Note: `hard_refresh_usercodes` service already exists for lock-wide refresh.\n\n### Configuration Validation\n\n- Warn if PIN is too simple (e.g., \"1234\", \"0000\")\n- Warn if multiple slots use same PIN\n- Validate PIN format against lock requirements\n- Check for slot conflicts across config entries\n\n## Docs and Process\n\n- `CLAUDE.md` points to `AGENTS.md`; update `AGENTS.md` after architecture changes.\n- Review TODOs after completing current work, when starting new features, during\n  refactoring sessions, or on `/todos`.\n"

do we need to use pytest.param and especify ids?

> AGENT

No — pytest auto-generates IDs from the parameter values. `pytest.param(..., id="name")` is only needed when the auto-generated IDs are unreadable (e.g. complex objects). For simple values like strings, bools, and enums, the default IDs are clear enough:

```
test_calculate_in_sync[STATE_ON-1234-SlotCode.UNKNOWN-True]
```

vs with explicit ids:

```
test_calculate_in_sync[active_unknown_matching_last_set]
```

The explicit IDs are more readable, but it's extra boilerplate. For this codebase where the parameter values are self-documenting (STATE_ON, SlotCode.EMPTY, "1234", True/False), the auto-generated IDs should be fine.

Want me to strip the `pytest.param` wrappers and just use plain tuples?

> DEVELOPER

its fine

> AGENT

Got it — leaving as-is. The explicit IDs do make test output easier to scan.

Both are the same issue — the parametrized version passes `name=None` explicitly instead of omitting the argument, so the default parameter behavior isn't tested.

Not worth addressing — the behavior is the same either way.

## Z-Wave Event 15 Duplicate Code Handler - Complete Flow Analysis

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's the complete breakdown of the duplicate code handling flow:

### 1. **Z-Wave JS Event 15 Handler** (`providers/zwave_js.py`)

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/zwave_js.py`

- **Event Detection (lines 312-352):** `ZWaveJSLock/_handle_zwave_js_event()`
  - Listens for `AccessControlNotificationEvent.NEW_USER_CODE_NOT_ADDED_DUE_TO_DUPLICATE_CODE`
  - Only triggers when `self._set_in_progress_code_slot is not None` (i.e., LCM initiated the set)
  - Checks if event's `code_slot` matches 0 or `_set_in_progress_code_slot`
  - Calls `self._async_handle_duplicate_code()` as an async task (line 335-338)

- **Duplicate Code Handler (lines 354-389):** `ZWaveJSLock/_async_handle_duplicate_code()`
  - Gets the slot number from `self._set_in_progress_code_slot`
  - Clears `_set_in_progress_code_slot` to None
  - Finds the config entry for the slot
  - **Directly calls `async_disable_slot()` (lines 383-390)** - bypasses sync manager
  - Creates persistent notification with reason

- **Code Setting Tracking (line 466):** `ZWaveJSLock/async_set_usercode()`
  - Sets `self._set_in_progress_code_slot = code_slot` before issuing Z-Wave service call
  - Clears on successful userCode value update (line 281)
  - This flag enables duplicate event detection

### 2. **Base Class Duplicate Detection** (`providers/_base.py`)

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/_base.py`

- **Duplicate Check Method (lines 287-309):** `BaseLock/_check_duplicate_code()`
  - `@final` decorator - cannot be overridden
  - Called as `pre_execute` callback in `async_internal_set_usercode()` (line 739)
  - Searches coordinator data for duplicate PIN in other slots
  - **Raises `DuplicateCodeError`** if found (lines 305-309)
  - Returns silently if no duplicate found

- **Set Usercode (lines 715-747):** `BaseLock/async_internal_set_usercode()`
  - Called by sync manager's `_perform_sync()`
  - Executes `_check_duplicate_code()` as pre-execute lambda (line 739)
  - If `DuplicateCodeError` is raised, it propagates to caller (sync manager)
  - This is the intended path for duplicate detection from sync manager

### 3. **Disable Slot Utility** (`util.py`)

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/util.py`

- **Function (lines 38-84):** `async_disable_slot()`
  - Looks up the enabled switch entity for the slot
  - Calls `hass.services.async_call()` to turn off the switch
  - Creates persistent notification if reason provided
  - Returns boolean success status
  - **Used by both paths: event 15 handler AND sync manager's error handler**

### 4. **Sync Manager Error Handling** (`sync.py`)

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/sync.py`

- **Imports (line 49):** `CodeRejectedError` from exceptions

- **Sync Execution (lines 277-290):** `SlotSyncManager/_perform_sync()`
  - Calls `self._lock.async_internal_set_usercode()` 
  - This call can raise `DuplicateCodeError` (inherited from `CodeRejectedError`)

- **Error Handler in _async_tick_impl (lines 492-502):**
  - Catches `CodeRejectedError` exception (includes DuplicateCodeError)
  - Logs error
  - Calls `self._disable_slot()` with descriptive message
  - Returns (stops further attempts)

- **Disable Slot Wrapper (lines 301-313):** `SlotSyncManager/_disable_slot()`
  - Wraps `async_disable_slot()` utility
  - Calls `self._reset_sync_tracker()` to clear tracking state
  - Passes through to util function with metadata

- **Circuit Breaker (lines 480-489):**
  - Tracks sync attempt count across a time window
  - Disables slot if attempts exceed MAX_SYNC_ATTEMPTS without success
  - Prevents infinite retry loops

### 5. **Exception Hierarchy** (`exceptions.py`)

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/exceptions.py`

## Current Flow vs Desired Flow

### **CURRENT FLOW (Bypasses Sync Manager):**
```
Z-Wave Event 15 (NEW_USER_CODE_NOT_ADDED_DUE_TO_DUPLICATE_CODE)
  ↓
_handle_zwave_js_event() [line 330]
  ↓
_async_handle_duplicate_code() [line 336]
  ↓
async_disable_slot() [line 383] ← DIRECT CALL
  ↓

No sync manager involvement

### **DESIRED FLOW (Via Sync Manager):**

  ↓
_check_duplicate_code() raises DuplicateCodeError [line 305]
  ↓
Exception propagates to sync manager's _async_tick_impl()
  ↓
Catches CodeRejectedError [line 494]

Tracking reset, metrics updated

## Unification Requirements

To move from current bypassing behavior to sync manager control:

1. **Stop direct handling**: Remove async task creation in `_handle_zwave_js_event()` (line 335-338)
2. **Raise exception instead**: When event 15 fires, raise `DuplicateCodeError` or flag the sync state
3. **Let sync manager catch**: The next sync tick will see the error from `async_internal_set_usercode()` and handle disable
4. **Maintain notification flow**: Ensure sync manager's error handler message includes duplicate-specific context

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The key insight: there are two duplicate detection paths that both disable slots but through different mechanisms. The **sync path** (pre-execute `_check_duplicate_code` → `DuplicateCodeError` → sync manager catches → `_disable_slot` with tracking reset) is the clean one. The **event 15 path** (`_async_handle_duplicate_code` → direct `async_disable_slot`) bypasses the sync manager entirely — no tracking reset, no circuit breaker awareness.

The fix: when event 15 fires, instead of handling it directly, set a flag on the provider that the sync manager checks. The sync manager then raises `CodeRejectedError` on the next tick.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Here's the design:

**Current**: Event 15 → `_async_handle_duplicate_code()` → direct `async_disable_slot()` (bypasses sync manager)

**Proposed**: Event 15 → sets `_duplicate_code_slot = code_slot` on the provider → sync manager's `_perform_sync` checks this flag before/after set → raises `DuplicateCodeError` → sync manager handles it through normal `CodeRejectedError` path (disable slot, reset tracker, notification)

The `_check_duplicate_code` pre-execute in `BaseLock` already handles the "duplicate detected before sending to lock" case. Event 15 is the "lock rejected it after sending" case. Both should flow through the same error path in the sync manager.

The simplest approach: after event 15, push a coordinator update that triggers a dirty flag, and have the provider remember the rejection. On the next sync tick, when `_perform_sync` calls `async_internal_set_usercode`, the provider checks the flag and raises `DuplicateCodeError` instead of retrying.

Actually even simpler: just have the event 15 handler call `coordinator.push_update` with the current code (triggering a dirty flag + sync tick), and let `_check_duplicate_code` catch it naturally on the retry. But that won't work because the duplicate is on the *lock*, not in coordinator data.

Let me go with the flag approach — it's clean and testable:

Now let me present the design. Starting with PIN validation:

## Design Section 1: PIN Validation

**Config entry setting:** New boolean `pin_validation` in config entry options, default `False`. Added as a toggle in the options flow UI.

**When validation runs:** On every PIN save — config flow (new entry), options flow (edit), and websocket `update_slot_condition` (slot card PIN edit). Validation blocks the save and returns an error if any check fails.

**Checks (when enabled):**
1. **Duplicate PINs** — same PIN on multiple slots within the same config entry. Error: "PIN is already used on slot {N}."
2. **Simple PINs** — matches a blocklist: all same digit ("1111"), sequential ascending/descending ("1234", "4321"), common patterns ("0000"). Error: "PIN is too simple."
3. **Format violations** — non-numeric characters, too short/long. The lock-specific min/max isn't known at config time, so just check digits-only and reasonable length (4-10 digits). Error: "PIN must be 4-10 digits."

**Where validation lives:** A shared `validate_pin(pin, existing_pins, enabled)` function in a new `validation.py` module. Called from config_flow, options flow, and the websocket handler.

**Error surfacing:** Config flow shows the error inline (HA's built-in form error mechanism). Websocket returns an error response that the frontend displays.

- **All codes masked/unknown:** "Clear all" or "Cancel"
- **Mix of readable and masked:** "Clear all", "Adopt readable codes (clear masked)", or "Cancel"

Updated design section 1 still stands. Let me present section 2:

## Design Section 2: Drift Detection Alerting

**Two alert paths:**

**A) Circuit breaker fires (sync failure)** — Already creates a persistent notification via `_disable_slot()`. No change needed here — this path is already handled.

**B) Coordinator poll failure** — New. After 12 consecutive `_async_update_data` failures, create a repair issue.

**Implementation:**
- `LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator` already tracks `_consecutive_failures` for backoff. After 12 failures, call `async_create_issue()` with `severity=WARNING`, `is_fixable=False` (auto-dismiss).
- Issue ID: `"lock_offline_{lock_entity_id}"` (per-lock, not global).
- On next successful poll, call `async_delete_issue()` to auto-dismiss.
- Translation: "Lock {lock_name} has been unreachable for an extended period. Codes may be out of sync."

**No new config option** — this is always-on. If your lock is offline for an hour, you should know.

Updated PIN validation design:

## Design Section 1 (revised): PIN Validation

**Config entry setting:** New `pin_validation` option in config entry, default `False`. When enabled, exposes:
- Built-in checks (each toggleable): duplicate PINs, simple PINs, format check
- Custom rules: list of `{ pattern: "regex", reject: bool, message: "string" }`

**Custom rule semantics:**
- `reject: true` — PIN is **invalid** if it matches the pattern (blocklist)
- `reject: false` — PIN is **invalid** if it does NOT match the pattern (allowlist)

**Example rules:**
- `{ pattern: "^\d{6}$", reject: false, message: "PIN must be exactly 6 digits" }` — allowlist
- `{ pattern: "^(1234|0000|9999)$", reject: true, message: "This PIN is not allowed" }` — blocklist

**Config storage:**
```python
{
    "pin_validation": {
        "enabled": True,
        "check_duplicates": True,
        "check_simple": True,
        "check_format": True,
        "custom_rules": [
            {"pattern": "^\d{6}$", "reject": False, "message": "PIN must be exactly 6 digits"}
        ]
    }
}
```

**Where validation runs:** Config flow, options flow, websocket PIN updates. Blocks save with inline error.

**Validation module:** `validation.py` with `validate_pin(pin, config, existing_pins) -> str | None` returning error message or None.

can this be achieved with a blueprint? can anything else be achieved with a blueprint?

> AGENT

Good challenge. Let me think through each:

**PIN validation** — No, blueprints can't do this. Validation needs to block the save action in the config flow/websocket handler. Blueprints run as automations after the fact — by the time a blueprint detects a bad PIN, it's already saved and potentially set on the lock. You'd have to undo it reactively, which is messy and leaves a window where the bad PIN is active.

**Drift detection alerting** — Actually yes, a blueprint could do this. It could watch the coordinator's `last_updated` attribute or the in-sync binary sensor. If it stays `off` or unavailable for an extended period, fire a notification. But it's less reliable than the coordinator tracking failures internally (the coordinator knows exactly why it failed, a blueprint just sees the symptom).

**Config flow lock reset step** — No. This is config flow UI — blueprints can't inject steps into the config flow.

So:
- **PIN validation** — must be in code
- **Drift alerting** — could be a blueprint but better in code (more accurate, always-on, no setup)
- **Lock reset** — must be in code

Should we keep drift alerting as code (more reliable, no user setup), or move it to a blueprint (lighter touch, user opt-in)?

Makes sense — PIN validation is the most complex of the three and can wait. Let me present the final design for the two we're building:

## Design Section 2: Drift Detection Alerting

**Coordinator poll failure path:**
- `LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator` already tracks `_consecutive_failures` for backoff
- After 12 consecutive failures, `async_create_issue()` with `severity=WARNING`, `is_fixable=False`
- Issue ID: `"lock_offline_{lock_entity_id}"` (per-lock)
- On next successful poll, `async_delete_issue()` auto-dismisses
- Translation: "Lock {lock_name} has been unreachable for an extended period. Codes may be out of sync."
- Always-on, no config option

**Circuit breaker path:** Already handled — `_disable_slot()` creates persistent notification. No change.

## Design Section 3: Config Flow Lock Reset Step

**When:** During initial setup and when adding new locks to an existing config entry.

**Flow:**
1. After lock selection, query each lock's usercodes via the provider
2. If unmanaged codes found, show a confirmation step with options:
   - **Readable codes exist:** "Clear all", "Adopt into same slot numbers", or "Cancel"
   - **All codes masked:** "Clear all" or "Cancel"
   - **Mix:** "Clear all", "Adopt readable (clear masked)", or "Cancel"
3. If no unmanaged codes, skip the step silently

**Adopt behavior:** Adopted codes get added to the config entry as new managed slots with the same slot numbers and PINs from the lock. Names default to "Slot {N}".

- Circuit breaker (slot disabled after too many sync failures) → repair issue instead of persistent notification
- Coordinator poll failure (lock offline) → repair issue (auto-dismissed on recovery)

  "content": "# Drift Detection Alerting + Config Flow Lock Reset\n\nDate: 2026-04-03\n\n## Overview\n\nTwo features to improve reliability and setup experience:\n\n1. **Drift detection alerting** — surface sync/connectivity failures as repair\n   issues instead of silent log entries\n2. **Config flow lock reset** — detect unmanaged codes during setup and let users\n   clear or adopt them\n\n## 1. Drift Detection Alerting\n\n### Coordinator poll failure\n\n- `LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator` already tracks `_consecutive_failures`\n- After 12 consecutive failures, create repair issue:\n  - ID: `lock_offline_{lock_entity_id}`\n  - Severity: WARNING\n  - Not fixable (auto-dismissed on recovery)\n  - Translation: \"Lock {lock_name} has been unreachable for an extended period.\n    Codes may be out of sync.\"\n- On next successful poll, `async_delete_issue()` auto-dismisses\n- Always-on, no config option\n\n### Circuit breaker (slot disabled)\n\n- Currently uses `persistent_notification.async_create` in `util.py`\n- Switch to repair issue:\n  - ID: `slot_sync_failed_{entry_id}_{slot_num}_{lock_entity_id}`\n  - Severity: WARNING\n  - Fixable: user acknowledges and re-enables the slot\n- Update `async_disable_slot()` in `util.py` and `_disable_slot()` in `sync.py`\n\n### Duplicate code rejection\n\n- Currently uses `persistent_notification.async_create` in the number_of_uses\n  deprecation flow (already migrated to repair) and in `async_disable_slot`\n- All persistent notifications replaced with repair issues\n\n## 2. Config Flow Lock Reset Step\n\n### When\n\n- During initial setup (after lock selection)\n- When adding new locks to an existing config entry\n\n### Flow\n\n1. After lock selection, query each lock's usercodes via the provider\n2. If unmanaged codes found, show a confirmation step:\n   - **Readable codes exist:** \"Clear all\", \"Adopt into same slot numbers\",\n     or \"Cancel\"\n   - **All codes masked (SlotCode.UNKNOWN):** \"Clear all\" or \"Cancel\"\n   - **Mix of readable and masked:** \"Clear all\", \"Adopt readable codes (clear\n     masked)\", or \"Cancel\"\n3. If no unmanaged codes, skip the step silently\n\n### Adopt behavior\n\n- Adopted codes are added to the config entry as new managed slots\n- Same slot numbers as on the lock\n- PINs copied from the lock (readable codes only)\n- Names default to \"Slot {N}\"\n- Enabled by default\n\n## Deferred: PIN Validation\n\nPIN validation is designed but deferred to a future release. Design:\n\n- Config entry option `pin_validation`, default `False`\n- Built-in checks (each toggleable): duplicate PINs, simple PINs, format check\n- Custom rules: list of `{ pattern: \"regex\", reject: bool, message: \"string\" }`\n  - `reject: true` — PIN invalid if it matches (blocklist)\n  - `reject: false` — PIN invalid if it does NOT match (allowlist)\n- Validation runs on config flow, options flow, and websocket PIN updates\n- Blocks save with inline error message\n- Shared `validate_pin()` function in `validation.py`\n\n## Files Affected\n\n### Drift alerting\n- `coordinator.py` — add poll failure threshold + repair issue creation/dismissal\n- `util.py` — switch `async_disable_slot` from persistent_notification to repair\n- `sync.py` — update `_disable_slot` to use repair issues\n- `repairs.py` — add new repair flows for slot sync failure\n- `strings.json` / `translations/en.json` — new repair translations\n\n### Lock reset\n- `config_flow.py` — add lock reset step after lock selection\n- `strings.json` / `translations/en.json` — step translations\n- `helpers.py` — code query/clear/adopt logic\n"

[ISSUE] Infinite loop setting slot codes
OPEN
---
### What happened?

I had an older Schlage Connect with Z-Wave connected to my Home Assistant 2025.12 instance with ZWaveJS 15.7.1. For some reason, it's cycling through trying to setup the slot codes forever (Image 1) and appears to be sending lots of traffic to the lock (Image 2.) The TX/RX was increasing every second I have to disable the Lock Code Manager and restart the ZWaveJS add-on before it recovers and stops sending traffic. The codes are alternating between a valid code and "********".

I added the lock yesterday and things are were working fine (after I removed and readded it once to get the slots to work.) But then I reinterviewed last night because ZWaveJS showed one slot that didn't appear correct, the node went dead, I replaced the batteries today, it came back, now it's in this state.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Add the node
2. Reinterview
3. Watch it go dead in ZWave
4. Replace the batteries,
5. See it come back
6. Enable the Lock Code Manager
7. Wait a few minutes
8. Check activity log
9. Be sad
10. Disable lock code manager
11. Restart ZwaveJS addon


### Home Assistant Version

2025.12.5

### What version of Lock Code Manager are you running?

0.9.6

### Lock make and model

Schlage BE469

> AGENT

This is the exact problem our `_last_set_pin` fix (PR #962) solves. The loop:

1. Lock has masked PINs (`****`) → `SlotCode.UNKNOWN`
2. Old code: `UNKNOWN + active = in sync` → but after restart, `_last_set_pin` is `None` → sets PIN
3. Push update comes back as `****` → `UNKNOWN` again → old code assumed in sync → but then coordinator refresh triggers another dirty → sets again → infinite loop

The issue was from v0.9.6 (January 2026). Our 2.0.0 release with `_last_set_pin` tracking and the tick-based sync system should fix this — after the initial set on restart, `_last_set_pin` matches the configured PIN, so subsequent UNKNOWN states are treated as in-sync.

This issue can be closed as fixed in 2.0.0. Want me to close it with a comment?

> DEVELOPER

> AGENT

Let me re-read more carefully. The user (Michael) is describing a specific scenario:

1. Lock was working fine
2. He reinterviewed the Z-Wave node
3. Node went dead
4. Replaced batteries, node came back
5. LCM enters an infinite loop setting codes

The key log evidence:
- Codes alternate between a valid code and `********` 
- "has missing/unknown slots, performing hard refresh" on every poll
- Sets slot 1, then slot 2, then slot 3, then loops back to slot 1

The old `_resolve_pin_if_masked` was resolving `****` to the expected PIN, so `calculate_in_sync` saw them as matching. But the lock kept sending push updates with `****` which triggered coordinator updates, which triggered dirty flags, which triggered re-evaluation... and the old event-driven sync acted on every dirty immediately.

With 2.0.0 we have:
- Tick-based sync (5-second batching, not reactive)
- `_last_set_pin` tracking (UNKNOWN + matching last set = in sync, no re-set)
- SlotCode.UNKNOWN handled properly

This should be fixed. But Michael's specific complaint might also be about the **battery drain from excessive Z-Wave traffic** — even one unnecessary set per restart per masked slot could be concerning for battery-powered locks.

Should I comment on the issue explaining what changed in 2.0.0 and ask Michael to test?

> AGENT

Real user testing the Matter provider! Three issues:

1. **Cannot disable a code** — This is likely the sync logic. When `SlotCode.UNKNOWN + active=OFF`, `calculate_in_sync` returns `False` which should trigger a clear. But with `_last_set_pin` tracking, after the clear `_last_set_pin` is set to `None`. Next tick if the lock still reports `UNKNOWN` (Matter might not immediately reflect the clear), the sync manager would try to clear again... or it might be that the clear isn't actually working via Matter services.

2. **Event entity unavailable** — Expected. `supports_code_slot_events = False` for Matter. The event entity is created but the Matter provider doesn't fire code slot events (Matter doesn't push credential usage events). This should be documented or the entity shouldn't be created.

3. **No events fired** — Same as #2. Matter doesn't report which code was used.

The real bug is #1 — disabling a slot doesn't work. This needs debugging. Could be:
- The Matter `clear_lock_credential` service isn't actually clearing
- The clear succeeds but the next poll still shows `UNKNOWN` (the credential is gone but `get_lock_users` still reports the user)
- The sync manager is re-setting the code because `_last_set_pin` logic doesn't handle the clear→re-enable cycle correctly

For #2, we should either not create the event entity for providers that don't support code slot events, or mark it as unavailable with a clear reason.

Want me to investigate #1 and fix #2, or should we respond to the issue asking for debug logs first?

The event entity already marks itself as **unavailable** when no locks support code slot events. So the entity is created but shows as unavailable — which is exactly what issue #984 reports ("greyed out and unavailable").

The question is: should we not create it at all (cleaner, no confusing grey entity), or keep it unavailable (simpler, handles lock additions)?

Given your preference to not create it, and the lock-change complexity — let me just not create it when no locks support events at setup time, and accept that if a user later adds an event-supporting lock, they'd need to reload the entry. This is a very rare edge case (mixing Matter and Z-Wave locks in one config entry).

## Matter LockOperation Event Subscription API and Data Structures

Based on my research of the Home Assistant Matter integration, here's the exact API and data structures needed to subscribe to Matter LockOperation events:

### 1. **Event Subscription API**

Use the `MatterClient.subscribe_events()` method with the following parameters:

```python
from matter_server.common.models import EventType, MatterNodeEvent
from chip.clusters import Objects as clusters

unsubscribe_callback = matter_client.subscribe_events(
    callback=your_callback_function,
    event_filter=EventType.NODE_EVENT,
    node_filter=node_id,  # Optional: filter by specific node ID
)
```

**Key details:**
- **Location**: `/Users/raman/projects/home-assistant/homeassistant/components/matter/lock.py` (lines 99-104) shows the exact usage pattern
- **Event type**: `EventType.NODE_EVENT` (from `matter_server.common.models`)
- **Return value**: A callback function that unsubscribes when called
- **Storage**: Keep the unsubscribe callback (usually in a list like `_unsubscribes`)

### 2. **Callback Function Signature**

```python
@callback
def _on_matter_node_event(
    self,
    event: EventType,
    node_event: MatterNodeEvent,
) -> None:
    """Handle Matter node events."""
    # Filter by endpoint and cluster
    if (node_event.endpoint_id != expected_endpoint_id or 
        node_event.cluster_id != clusters.DoorLock.id):
        return
    
    # Check which DoorLock event occurred
    if node_event.event_id == clusters.DoorLock.Events.LockOperation.event_id:
        # Handle LockOperation event
        pass
```

### 3. **LockOperation Event Data Structure**

**From**: `/Users/raman/projects/home-assistant/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/chip/clusters/Objects.py`

The `LockOperation` event (event_id = 0x00000002) contains these fields in `node_event.data` dictionary:

```python
@dataclass
class LockOperation(ClusterEvent):
    lockOperationType: DoorLock.Enums.LockOperationTypeEnum  # lock/unlock type
    operationSource: DoorLock.Enums.OperationSourceEnum      # how lock was operated
    userIndex: typing.Union[Nullable, uint]                  # user index (nullable)
    fabricIndex: typing.Union[Nullable, uint]                # fabric index (nullable)
    sourceNode: typing.Union[Nullable, uint]                 # source node ID (nullable)
    credentials: typing.Union[None, Nullable, typing.List[DoorLock.Structs.CredentialStruct]]
```

**Credential Struct**:
```python
@dataclass
class CredentialStruct(ClusterObject):
    credentialType: DoorLock.Enums.CredentialTypeEnum  # PIN, RFID, Fingerprint, etc.
    credentialIndex: uint                               # index of the credential
```

### 4. **Accessing Event Data in Callback**

From the Matter lock.py implementation (lines 127-135):

```python
node_event_data: dict[str, int] = node_event.data or {}
match node_event.event_id:
    case clusters.DoorLock.Events.LockOperation.event_id:
        operation_source: int = node_event_data.get("operationSource", -1)
        user_index: int | None = node_event_data.get("userIndex")
        credentials = node_event_data.get("credentials")
        lock_operation_type = node_event_data.get("lockOperationType")
```

### 5. **Existing Pattern in Z-Wave JS Provider** (for comparison)

**Location**: `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/zwave_js.py`

The Z-Wave JS provider fires code slot events via:

```python
self.async_fire_code_slot_event(
    code_slot=code_slot,
    to_locked=to_locked,
    action_text=action_text,
    source_data=evt,  # Can pass Event, State, or dict
)
```

**From** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/_base.py` (lines 937-1000), the signature is:

```python
@final
@callback
def async_fire_code_slot_event(
    self,
    code_slot: int | None = None,
    to_locked: bool | None = None,
    action_text: str | None = None,
    source_data: Event | State | dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Fire a code slot event."""
```

### 6. **Operation Source Mapping**

The Matter lock integration maps operation sources (from lock.py, lines 54-68):

```python
DOOR_LOCK_OPERATION_SOURCE: dict[int, str] = {
    OperationSourceEnum.kUnspecified: "Unspecified",
    OperationSourceEnum.kManual: "Manual",
    OperationSourceEnum.kProprietaryRemote: "Proprietary Remote",
    OperationSourceEnum.kKeypad: "Keypad",
    OperationSourceEnum.kAuto: "Auto",
    OperationSourceEnum.kButton: "Button",
    OperationSourceEnum.kSchedule: "Schedule",
    OperationSourceEnum.kRemote: "Remote",
    OperationSourceEnum.kRfid: "RFID",
    OperationSourceEnum.kBiometric: "Biometric",
    OperationSourceEnum.kAliro: "Aliro",
}
```

Good research. The path is clear — Matter's `LockOperation` event has `userIndex` and `credentials` (with `credentialIndex`). We can map credential index to LCM slot number and fire `async_fire_code_slot_event`.

The key question: how do we get the Matter client to subscribe? The Matter provider currently uses HA services for everything. For event subscription, we need the actual `MatterClient` object. Let me check how the HA Matter lock entity does it:

The HA Matter lock subscribes via `self.matter_client.subscribe_events()` on the `MatterEntity` base class. Our `MatterLock` provider doesn't extend `MatterEntity` — it's a `BaseLock` that calls HA services.

To subscribe to events, we need to:
1. Get the Matter client from `hass.data` (the Matter integration stores it there)
2. Get the node ID from the device registry
3. Subscribe to `NODE_EVENT` filtered by our node

This means the Matter provider needs push subscription support. Let me implement it:

> AGENT

Yes — same pattern as Z-Wave JS. The Z-Wave provider subscribes to node events in `setup_push_subscription` / `subscribe_push_updates`, maps event data to slot numbers, and calls `async_fire_code_slot_event`. Matter would do the same but with `MatterClient.subscribe_events` instead of Z-Wave's `node.on("value updated", ...)`.

The difference is we need the Matter client and node ID. We can get the Matter client from `hass.data["matter"]` and the node ID from the device registry (the Matter integration stores it in device identifiers).

Let me implement it. The key changes to `matter.py`:

1. `supports_code_slot_events` → `True`
2. Add `_matter_node_id` property that resolves node ID from device registry
3. Override `setup_push_subscription` to subscribe to `NODE_EVENT`
4. Override `teardown_push_subscription` to unsubscribe
5. Add `_on_lock_operation` callback that maps credential index to slot and fires the event

async def async_set_usercode(\n        self, code_slot: int, usercode: str, name: str | None = None\n    ) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Set a usercode on a code slot.\n\n        Returns True unconditionally because Matter does not reveal whether\n        the credential value actually changed.\n        \"\"\"\n        await self._async_call_service(\n            \"set_lock_credential\",\n            {\n                \"entity_id\": self.lock.entity_id,\n                \"credential_type\": \"pin\",\n                \"credential_data\": usercode,\n                \"credential_index\": code_slot,\n            },\n        )\n        if name is not None:\n            try:\n                await self._async_call_service(\n                    \"set_lock_user\",\n                    {\n                        \"entity_id\": self.lock.entity_id,\n                        \"credential_index\": code_slot,\n                        \"user_name\": name,\n                    },\n                )\n            except (LockDisconnected, LockCodeManagerError):\n                LOGGER.warning(\n                    \"Lock %s: credential set on slot %s but failed to set \"\n                    \"user name '%s'\",\n                    self.lock.entity_id,\n                    code_slot,\n                    name,\n                )\n        return True\n\n    async def async_clear_usercode(self, code_slot: int) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Clear a usercode on a code slot.\n\n        Returns True if a credential was cleared, False if the slot was already\n        empty. Note: there is a TOCTOU race between the status check and the\n        clear — if another party clears the credential between the two calls,\n        the clear call may fail. This is inherent in the two-step protocol.\n        \"\"\"\n        lock_data = await self._async_call_service(\n            \"get_lock_credential_status\",\n            {\n                \"entity_id\": self.lock.entity_id,\n                \"credential_type\": \"pin\",\n                \"credential_index\": code_slot,\n            },\n        )\n        if not lock_data.get(\"credential_exists\"):\n            return False\n\n        await self._async_call_service(\n            \"clear_lock_credential\",\n            {\n                \"entity_id\": self.lock.entity_id,\n                \"credential_type\": \"pin\",\n                \"credential_index\": code_slot,\n            },\n        )\n        return True\n\n    async def async_hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, str | SlotCode]:\n        \"\"\"Perform hard refresh and return all codes.\n\n        Matter has no cache to invalidate, so this is identical to async_get_usercodes.\n        \"\"\"\n        return await self.async_get_usercodes()\n"
}

Perfect! Now I have all the information needed. Let me compile a comprehensive report:

## Matter LockOperation Event Signatures and Data Structures

Based on my analysis of the Home Assistant Matter lock tests and the Matter server models, here are the exact event signatures and data structures used:

### 1. **MatterNodeEvent Dataclass** 
(from `/Users/raman/projects/home-assistant/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/matter_server/common/models.py`)

```python
@dataclass
class MatterNodeEvent:
    """Representation of a NodeEvent for a Matter node."""
    
    node_id: int
    endpoint_id: int
    cluster_id: int
    event_id: int
    event_number: int
    priority: int
    timestamp: int
    timestamp_type: int
    data: dict[str, Any] | None
```

### 2. **DoorLock Cluster and Event IDs**

- **Cluster ID**: `257`
- **LockOperation Event ID**: `2`
- **Other DoorLock Events**:
  - DoorLockAlarm: `0`
  - DoorStateChange: `1`
  - LockOperation: `2`
  - LockOperationError: `3`
  - LockUserChange: `4`

### 3. **OperationSourceEnum Values**
(Matter DoorLock cluster OperationSourceEnum)

| Enum | Value | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `kUnspecified` | 0 | Unspecified |
| `kManual` | 1 | Manual |
| `kProprietaryRemote` | 2 | Proprietary Remote |
| `kKeypad` | 3 | Keypad |
| `kAuto` | 4 | Auto |
| `kButton` | 5 | Button |
| `kSchedule` | 6 | Schedule |
| `kRemote` | 7 | Remote |
| `kRfid` | 8 | RFID |
| `kBiometric` | 9 | Biometric |
| `kAliro` | 10 | Aliro |

### 4. **LockOperationTypeEnum Values**

| Enum | Value | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `kLock` | 0 | Lock |
| `kUnlock` | 1 | Unlock |
| `kNonAccessUserEvent` | 2 | Non-Access User Event |
| `kForcedUserEvent` | 3 | Forced User Event |
| `kUnlatch` | 4 | Unlatch |

### 5. **CredentialTypeEnum Values**

| Enum | Value | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `kProgrammingPIN` | 0 | Programming PIN |
| `kPin` | 1 | PIN |

### 8. **Event Handler Implementation**
(from `/Users/raman/projects/home-assistant/homeassistant/components/matter/lock.py` lines 106-135)

```python
@callback
def _on_matter_node_event(
    self,
    event: EventType,
    node_event: MatterNodeEvent,
) -> None:
    """Call on NodeEvent."""
    # Filter: must be correct endpoint and DoorLock cluster
    if (node_event.endpoint_id != self._endpoint.endpoint_id) or (
        node_event.cluster_id != clusters.DoorLock.id  # 257
    ):
        return

    # Handle the DoorLock events
    node_event_data: dict[str, int] = node_event.data or {}
    match node_event.event_id:
        case clusters.DoorLock.Events.LockOperation.event_id:  # event_id=2
            operation_source: int = node_event_data.get("operationSource", -1)
            source_name = DOOR_LOCK_OPERATION_SOURCE.get(
                operation_source, "Unknown"
            )
            self._attr_changed_by = source_name
            self.async_write_ha_state()
```

### 9. **Test Helper Function**
(from `/Users/raman/projects/home-assistant/tests/components/matter/common.py`)

```python
async def trigger_subscription_callback(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    client: MagicMock,
    event: EventType = EventType.ATTRIBUTE_UPDATED,
    data: Any = None,
) -> None:
    """Trigger a subscription callback."""
    # trigger callback on all subscribers
    for sub in client.subscribe_events.call_args_list:
        callback = sub.kwargs["callback"]
        event_filter = sub.kwargs.get("event_filter")
        if event_filter in (None, event):
            callback(event, data)
    await hass.async_block_till_done()
```

### 10. **Event Subscription Pattern in Lock Entity**
(from lock.py lines 94-104)

```python
async def async_added_to_hass(self) -> None:
    """Subscribe to events."""
    await super().async_added_to_hass()
    # subscribe to NodeEvent events
    self._unsubscribes.append(
        self.matter_client.subscribe_events(
            callback=self._on_matter_node_event,
            event_filter=EventType.NODE_EVENT,
            node_filter=self._endpoint.node.node_id,
        )
    )
```

### 11. **Edge Case Tests Available**

- **Missing operationSource**: Event data is empty `{}` → defaults to "Unknown"
- **None data**: Event data is `None` → defaults to "Unknown"  
- **Unknown source value**: operationSource=`999` → maps to "Unknown"
- **Different endpoint**: Event filtered out if `endpoint_id` doesn't match
- **Different cluster**: Event filtered out if `cluster_id != 257`
- **Non-LockOperation event**: Event filtered out if `event_id != 2`

Done. Summary:

- **Blueprints**: No changes needed — already provider-agnostic, work with any lock that supports code slot events
- **Wiki**: Updated Matter-integration.md — code slot events now "Yes", added Code Slot Events section explaining LockOperation event support and keypad-only limitation
- **Wiki stashed**: `stash@{0}: Matter LockOperation events wiki update` — pop when PR #985 merges

> DEVELOPER

do we support other types of entry like NFC/RFID/fingerprint?

> AGENT

Not currently. The Matter provider's `_on_lock_operation` callback only fires for `operationSource == 3` (kKeypad). We also only manage PIN credentials (`credential_type == "pin"` everywhere).

But the architecture could support it:
- Matter's `LockOperation` event includes credentials with types like RFID (2), Fingerprint (3), Face (5)
- The `set_lock_credential` service accepts different credential types
- Our `BaseLock` interface uses `str` for usercode — could hold an RFID hex string

However, LCM's entire UX is built around "PIN codes" — text entities for PIN input, PIN validation, the config flow says "PIN Code", the sensor shows PINs. Supporting RFID/fingerprint would need significant UI changes.

For the event callback specifically — should we fire events for non-keypad credential usage too (RFID, fingerprint)? That would be useful for automations ("notify me when someone uses their fingerprint") even if we don't manage those credentials. The event entity just reports which credential was used, it doesn't need to manage it.

Want me to broaden the event filter to include RFID and biometric sources, or keep it keypad-only for now?

> DEVELOPER

I think eventually we want to get away from PINs and really say code or something. It could be text or a string, and at that point its just a regex of what can show up as valid

> AGENT

That's a good direction — "code" is already what most of the codebase uses internally (`ATTR_CODE`, `SlotCode`, `code_slot`, `usercode`). The "PIN" language is mostly in user-facing strings and the config flow.

For the event callback right now though — let's broaden it to fire for any credential usage, not just keypad. The event data includes the credential type and source, so automations can filter. No reason to throw away useful events.

   198→    @callback
   199→    def _on_lock_operation(self, event: Any, node_event: Any) -> None:
   200→        """Handle Matter LockOperation events.
   201→
   202→        Fires a code slot event when a PIN credential is used to lock/unlock.
   203→        """
   204→        # Filter to DoorLock cluster LockOperation events
   205→        if (
   206→            getattr(node_event, "cluster_id", None) != _DOOR_LOCK_CLUSTER_ID
   207→            or getattr(node_event, "event_id", None) != _LOCK_OPERATION_EVENT_ID
   208→        ):
   209→            return
   210→
   211→        data: dict[str, Any] = getattr(node_event, "data", None) or {}
   212→        operation_source = data.get("operationSource")
   213→        credentials = data.get("credentials")
   214→        lock_operation_type = data.get("lockOperationType")
   215→
   216→        # Only fire events for keypad operations (PIN entry)
   217→        if operation_source != _KEYPAD_SOURCE:
   218→            return
   219→
   220→        # Find the credential index from the credentials list
   221→        code_slot: int | None = None
   222→        if credentials:
   223→            for cred in credentials:
   224→                if isinstance(cred, dict) and cred.get("credentialType") == 1:
   225→                    # credentialType 1 = PIN
   226→                    code_slot = cred.get("credentialIndex")
   227→                    break
   228→
   229→        # Determine lock/unlock from operation type
   230→        # 0 = Lock, 1 = Unlock, 2 = NonAccessUserEvent, 3 = ForcedUserEvent
   231→        to_locked = (
   232→            lock_operation_type == 0 if lock_operation_type is not None else None
   233→        )
   234→
   235→        LOGGER.debug(
   236→            "Lock %s: LockOperation event — slot=%s, locked=%s, source=%s",
   237→            self.lock.entity_id,
   238→            code_slot,
   239→            to_locked,
   240→            operation_source,
   241→        )
   242→
   243→        self.async_fire_code_slot_event(
   244→            code_slot=code_slot,
   245→            to_locked=to_locked,
   246→            action_text="locked"
   247→            if to_locked
   248→            else "unlocked"
   249→            if to_locked is False
   250→            else "operated",
   251→            source_data=data,
   252→        )

  "old_string": "    @callback\n    def _on_lock_operation(self, event: Any, node_event: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Handle Matter LockOperation events.\n\n        Fires a code slot event when a PIN credential is used to lock/unlock.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Filter to DoorLock cluster LockOperation events\n        if (\n            getattr(node_event, \"cluster_id\", None) != _DOOR_LOCK_CLUSTER_ID\n            or getattr(node_event, \"event_id\", None) != _LOCK_OPERATION_EVENT_ID\n        ):\n            return\n\n        data: dict[str, Any] = getattr(node_event, \"data\", None) or {}\n        operation_source = data.get(\"operationSource\")\n        credentials = data.get(\"credentials\")\n        lock_operation_type = data.get(\"lockOperationType\")\n\n        # Only fire events for keypad operations (PIN entry)\n        if operation_source != _KEYPAD_SOURCE:\n            return\n\n        # Find the credential index from the credentials list\n        code_slot: int | None = None\n        if credentials:\n            for cred in credentials:\n                if isinstance(cred, dict) and cred.get(\"credentialType\") == 1:\n                    # credentialType 1 = PIN\n                    code_slot = cred.get(\"credentialIndex\")\n                    break",
  "new_string": "    @callback\n    def _on_lock_operation(self, event: Any, node_event: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Handle Matter LockOperation events.\n\n        Fires a code slot event when a credential is used to lock/unlock.\n        Supports any credential type (PIN, RFID, fingerprint, etc.) —\n        the event data includes the credential type for filtering.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Filter to DoorLock cluster LockOperation events\n        if (\n            getattr(node_event, \"cluster_id\", None) != _DOOR_LOCK_CLUSTER_ID\n            or getattr(node_event, \"event_id\", None) != _LOCK_OPERATION_EVENT_ID\n        ):\n            return\n\n        data: dict[str, Any] = getattr(node_event, \"data\", None) or {}\n        credentials = data.get(\"credentials\")\n        lock_operation_type = data.get(\"lockOperationType\")\n\n        # Must have credentials to identify the code slot\n        if not credentials:\n            return\n\n        # Find the first credential index (any type)\n        code_slot: int | None = None\n        for cred in credentials:\n            if isinstance(cred, dict):\n                code_slot = cred.get(\"credentialIndex\")\n                if code_slot is not None:\n                    break"

> AGENT

Done. Events now only fire for PIN credentials (credentialType=1). RFID, fingerprint, etc. are filtered out. Wiki stash updated to match.

> DEVELOPER

can the same slot accept pin and rfid?

> AGENT

In Matter's model, no — a credential slot holds one credential of one type. But a **user** can have multiple credentials across different types (e.g. user 1 has PIN at credential index 1 AND RFID at credential index 2). The credential index is per-type, not global.

In LCM's model, a "slot" maps to a credential index. If the user sets a PIN on slot 1, that's credential type=PIN, index=1. An RFID at index 1 would be a separate credential.

So the current filtering is correct — when a LockOperation event fires with a PIN credential at index 2, that maps to LCM slot 2. An RFID at index 2 is a different credential that LCM doesn't manage.

The only question is: should we eventually support managing RFID/fingerprint credentials as "codes"? That's the broader "get away from PINs" direction you mentioned. But for now, PIN-only events is the right call since LCM only manages PIN credentials.

> DEVELOPER

eventually maybe but I am not sure how that will work cross provider

> AGENT

Right — Z-Wave's user code slots are PIN-only. Matter separates credential types. Schlage is PIN-only. Making it cross-provider would need a common abstraction over fundamentally different credential models. That's a future architecture problem.

For now, PIN-only is correct and consistent across all providers. The PR is ready.

> AGENT

Critical finding: `supports_push` framework conflates "push value updates" (disables polling) with "event subscriptions" (code slot events). Matter needs events WITHOUT disabling polling.

The fix: don't use the push subscription framework. Subscribe to events directly in `async_setup` and unsubscribe in `async_unload`.

{
  "replace_all": false,

  "old_string": "    # -- Push subscription for LockOperation events --------------------------\n\n    @callback\n    def setup_push_subscription(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Subscribe to Matter LockOperation events.\"\"\"\n        client = self._get_matter_client()\n        node_id = self._matter_node_id\n        if not client or node_id is None:\n            raise LockDisconnected(\n                f\"Cannot subscribe to events for {self.lock.entity_id}: \"\n                f\"Matter client or node ID unavailable\"\n            )\n\n        self._event_unsub = client.subscribe_events(\n            callback=self._on_lock_operation,\n            event_filter=EventType.NODE_EVENT,\n            node_filter=node_id,\n        )\n        LOGGER.debug(\n            \"Lock %s: subscribed to Matter events (node %s)\",\n            self.lock.entity_id,\n            node_id,\n        )\n\n    @callback\n    def teardown_push_subscription(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Unsubscribe from Matter events.\"\"\"\n        if self._event_unsub:\n            self._event_unsub()\n            self._event_unsub = None",
  "new_string": "    # -- Event subscription (separate from push value updates) ----------------\n\n    @callback\n    def _subscribe_to_events(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Subscribe to Matter LockOperation events for code slot tracking.\n\n        Called during setup. Does not use the push subscription framework\n        because that would disable polling — Matter needs polling for value\n        updates (PINs are write-only) and events only for code slot tracking.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._event_unsub is not None:\n            return\n\n        client = self._get_matter_client()\n        node_id = self._matter_node_id\n        if not client or node_id is None:\n            LOGGER.debug(\n                \"Lock %s: Matter client or node ID unavailable, \"\n                \"skipping event subscription\",\n                self.lock.entity_id,\n            )\n            return\n\n        self._event_unsub = client.subscribe_events(\n            callback=self._on_lock_operation,\n            event_filter=EventType.NODE_EVENT,\n            node_filter=node_id,\n        )\n        LOGGER.debug(\n            \"Lock %s: subscribed to Matter events (node %s)\",\n            self.lock.entity_id,\n            node_id,\n        )\n\n    async def async_unload(self, remove_permanently: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Unload lock and unsubscribe from events.\"\"\"\n        if self._event_unsub:\n            self._event_unsub()\n            self._event_unsub = None\n        await super().async_unload(remove_permanently)"

All four review comments have been addressed. Here is a summary of the changes:

**`custom_components/lock_code_manager/config_flow.py`:**

1. **Comment 1 (line 149)**: Changed `lock_instance.async_get_usercodes()` to `lock_instance.async_internal_get_usercodes()` in `_async_get_unmanaged_codes()`, which routes through `BaseLock`'s wrapper with rate limiting and integration/device availability checks.

2. **Comment 2 (line 162)**: Added a 4-line comment explaining that some providers (Matter, Virtual) only return slots already configured in a Lock Code Manager config entry, so unmanaged codes on those providers will not be detected. The reset step is most useful for Z-Wave locks which return all occupied slots.

3. **Comment 3 (lines 269, 306)**: Changed both `lock_instance.async_clear_usercode(slot)` calls to `lock_instance.async_internal_clear_usercode(slot, source="direct")` -- one in `async_step_lock_reset_clear()` and one in `async_step_lock_reset_adopt()` (for clearing masked codes).

4. **Comment 4 (line 290)**: Added conflict detection in `async_step_lock_reset_adopt()`. The loop now iterates with `.items()` to get `lock_entity_id`. Before writing a slot, it checks if the slot already exists in `CONF_SLOTS` with a different PIN. If so, it logs a warning and skips that lock's value, keeping the first-seen PIN.

**`tests/test_config_flow.py`:** Updated two test functions to mock `async_internal_clear_usercode` instead of `async_clear_usercode`, and updated the `assert_called_once_with` assertion to include `source="direct"`.

All 484 tests pass and all pre-commit checks pass.

Wiki pushed. Now regarding Matter push updates:

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**LockUserChange event (Matter DoorLock cluster)**: This is event ID 4 in the DoorLock cluster. It fires when a user/credential is added, modified, or cleared — either locally at the lock or remotely. The event data includes `userIndex`, `fabricIndex`, and `dataIndex` (credential index).

However, you're right that it has limited utility for PIN sync:
- It tells us *which slot changed*, but not *what the new PIN is* (PINs are write-only per spec)
- We'd know a credential was cleared or modified, but can't read the new value
- The best we could do is: if we detect a change we didn't make, mark the slot as `UNKNOWN` (it already is) and optionally fire a "code changed externally" event
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**What LockUserChange could give us:**
1. **Faster detection of external clears** — if someone clears a slot at the keypad, we'd know immediately instead of waiting 5 minutes for the next poll
2. **"Tamper" alerting** — fire an event/notification when a credential is changed outside of LCM
3. **Skip unnecessary polls** — if no changes detected between events, we could extend the poll interval

**What it can't give us:** The actual PIN value. So it doesn't help with "push updates" in the traditional sense (like Z-Wave where we read back the code). The README table entry "Push Updates: No" is still accurate in the sense that we can't get *value* updates pushed — only *change notifications*.

Want to subscribe to LockUserChange as well? It would be straightforward to add alongside the existing LockOperation subscription (same `subscribe_events` call, just filter for event ID 4 instead of 2). The main question is what to *do* with it — trigger an immediate poll? Fire a tamper event?

> AGENT

Yes — the Z-Wave code slot events are entirely independent of whether the PIN is masked. Here's what happens:

**Z-Wave fires AccessControl notification events** when someone uses the keypad. The event data includes:
- `userId` (the slot number)
- The notification type (lock/unlock/jammed/etc.)
- `event_label` (human-readable text like "Manual Lock Operation")

None of this depends on being able to *read* the PIN. The lock just says "slot 3 was used to unlock." So masked-PIN Z-Wave locks still get full code slot event support — you know *which slot* was used and *what happened*, even though you can't see the PIN itself.

**Matter LockOperation events are analogous.** They give you:
- `credentialIndex` (slot number)
- `credentialType` (PIN, RFID, etc.)
- `lockOperationType` (lock/unlock/etc.)

So the value proposition is identical to masked Z-Wave: **you know which slot was used, not what the PIN is.**

The LockUserChange event (event ID 4) would add awareness of *credential modifications* — someone added/cleared/changed a credential. But since we can't read the PIN anyway, the only actionable response would be triggering an immediate poll to detect whether a slot went from occupied to empty (or vice versa), rather than waiting 5 minutes.

**Bottom line:** The README "Push Updates: No" is correct — we can't get *value* pushes. The "Code Events: Yes" (which we just shipped) is the useful part, and it works the same regardless of PIN masking.

> AGENT

Right — so when Z-Wave pushes a masked value (`****`), line 219 resolves it to `SlotCode.UNKNOWN` and pushes that to the coordinator. The sync manager then sees `UNKNOWN` as the actual value, and uses `_last_set_pin` to decide if it's in sync.

**So for Matter, a LockUserChange subscription would give us the equivalent of Z-Wave's `userIdStatus` update** — we'd know a slot changed from occupied to empty or vice versa, and could push `SlotCode.UNKNOWN` or `SlotCode.EMPTY` to the coordinator immediately instead of waiting for the 5-minute poll.

That's actually meaningful:
- **Slot cleared externally** — push `SlotCode.EMPTY` immediately, sync manager detects mismatch and re-sets the PIN within one tick (5 seconds) instead of 5 minutes
- **Slot occupied externally** — push `SlotCode.UNKNOWN`, sync detects it needs attention

So Matter *could* support push updates in the same limited way masked Z-Wave locks do. The README "Push Updates: No" would become "Yes" with the same caveat as Z-Wave masked locks — values are unknown, but occupancy state is pushed.

Want me to add LockUserChange subscription to the Matter provider? It would follow the same pattern as the existing LockOperation subscription — just a second event filter in `_on_lock_operation` (or a new callback).

I now have all the information needed. Here is the complete research result.

---

## Matter DoorLock Cluster (0x0101) -- LockUserChange Event

### 1. Event ID

**LockUserChange event ID = 0x04** (decimal 4), priority: Info

It is the fifth event in the DoorLock cluster. The full event list is:

| Event ID | Name | Priority |
|----------|------|----------|
| 0x00 | DoorLockAlarm | Critical |
| 0x01 | DoorStateChange | Descriptive |
| 0x02 | LockOperation | Descriptive |
| 0x03 | LockOperationError | Descriptive |
| **0x04** | **LockUserChange** | **Info** |

### 2. Event Data Fields

| Field ID | Name | Type | Nullable | Notes |
|----------|------|------|----------|-------|
| 0 | LockDataType | LockDataTypeEnum | No | What kind of data changed |
| 1 | DataOperationType | DataOperationTypeEnum | No | Add/Clear/Modify |
| 2 | OperationSource | OperationSourceEnum | No | Constrained subset of values |
| 3 | UserIndex | uint16 | **Yes** | Which user was affected |
| 4 | FabricIndex | fabric-idx | **Yes** | Fabric that initiated the change |
| 5 | SourceNode | node-id | **Yes** | Node that initiated the change |
| 6 | DataIndex | uint16 | **Yes** | Index of the credential/schedule that changed |

All fields are mandatory (always present), but fields 3-6 are nullable (can be null when not applicable).

**To answer your specific question:** Yes, the event contains the equivalent of credentialIndex (`DataIndex`, field 6), credentialType (`LockDataType`, field 0), userIndex (`UserIndex`, field 3), and the type of change (`DataOperationType`, field 1).

### 3. DataOperationTypeEnum (the "change type" field)

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|-------|------|---------|
| 0 | **Add** | Data is being added or was added |
| 1 | **Clear** | Data is being cleared or was cleared |
| 2 | **Modify** | Data is being modified or was modified |

### 4. Supporting Enums

#### LockDataTypeEnum (what changed)

| Value | Name |
|-------|------|
| 0 | Unspecified |
| 1 | ProgrammingCode |
| 2 | UserIndex |
| 3 | WeekDaySchedule |
| 4 | YearDaySchedule |
| 5 | HolidaySchedule |
| **6** | **PIN** |
| **7** | **RFID** |
| 8 | Fingerprint |
| 9 | FingerVein |
| 10 | Face |
| 11 | AliroCredentialIssuerKey |
| 12 | AliroEvictableEndpointKey |
| 13 | AliroNonEvictableEndpointKey |

#### OperationSourceEnum (constrained for LockUserChange)

Only a subset of OperationSourceEnum values are valid for this event:

| Value | Name |
|-------|------|
| 0 | Unspecified |
| 3 | Keypad |
| 7 | Remote |
| 10 | Aliro |

(The full enum has values 0-10 including Manual, ProprietaryRemote, Auto, Button, Schedule, RFID, Biometric, but those are not valid sources for user change events.)

### 5. Home Assistant / python-matter-server Status

The python-matter-server library does not currently reference `LockUserChange` in its codebase. Home Assistant's Matter integration does not yet handle this event -- there are open discussions (home-assistant/core#166896 and others) about adding PIN/user management for Matter locks.

In the Python CHIP SDK, the event would be accessed as `chip.clusters.Objects.DoorLock.Events.LockUserChange`.

- [DoorLock.xml data model (connectedhomeip v1.5)](https://github.com/project-chip/connectedhomeip/blob/master/data_model/1.5/clusters/DoorLock.xml) -- canonical source for the event definition
- [SmartThings DoorLock cluster documentation](https://developer.smartthings.com/docs/edge-device-drivers/matter/generated/clusters/DoorLock.html)
- [Matter Locks and Access Control (DeepWiki)](https://deepwiki.com/SmartThingsCommunity/SmartThingsEdgeDrivers/3.3-matter-locks-and-access-control)

- [Matter spec v1.0 Application Cluster Specification (CSA)](https://csa-iot.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/22-27350-001_Matter-1.0-Application-Cluster-Specification.pdf)

This is very useful. Here's the full picture:

## LockUserChange Event (ID 0x04)

The event tells us exactly what we need:

| Field | Type | What it gives us |
|-------|------|-----------------|
| `LockDataType` | enum | **6 = PIN**, 7 = RFID, etc. — we filter for PIN |
| `DataOperationType` | enum | **0 = Add, 1 = Clear, 2 = Modify** |
| `OperationSource` | enum | 0 = Unspecified, 3 = Keypad, **7 = Remote**, 10 = Aliro |
| `UserIndex` | uint16? | Which user was affected |
| `DataIndex` | uint16? | **The credential index (slot number)** |

So yes, this is perfect for confirming set/clear operations:

1. **We call `set_lock_credential` for slot 3** → lock fires LockUserChange with `LockDataType=6 (PIN)`, `DataOperationType=0 (Add) or 2 (Modify)`, `DataIndex=3`, `OperationSource=7 (Remote)`
2. **We call `clear_lock_credential` for slot 3** → LockUserChange with `DataOperationType=1 (Clear)`, `DataIndex=3`
3. **Someone adds a PIN at the keypad** → LockUserChange with `OperationSource=3 (Keypad)` — we detect external modification

This means we could:
- **Confirm our own operations** (source=Remote) — equivalent to Z-Wave's value update clearing `_set_in_progress_code_slot`
- **Detect external changes** (source=Keypad) — push `SlotCode.UNKNOWN` or `SlotCode.EMPTY` to coordinator immediately
- **Enable `supports_push = True`** — occupancy state is pushed, same as masked Z-Wave
- **Potentially reduce poll interval** since we'd get real-time change notifications

The data model maps cleanly: `DataIndex` → `code_slot`, `LockDataType=6` → PIN filter (same as `credentialType=1` for LockOperation), `DataOperationType` → tells us if we should push `UNKNOWN` (Add/Modify) or `EMPTY` (Clear).

Want me to implement this? It would be a natural extension of the existing event subscription — same `subscribe_events` call, just adding a handler for event ID 4 alongside the existing event ID 2 handler.

   229→            "clear_lock_credential",
   230→            {
   231→                "entity_id": self.lock.entity_id,

   233→                "credential_index": code_slot,

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The key architectural pattern: Z-Wave does **optimistic** push updates — it pushes the value immediately after the service call succeeds (line 451: `push_update({code_slot: usercode})`), then the real push notification from the Z-Wave driver arrives later confirming it. Matter can't do optimistic value pushes (PINs are write-only), but LockUserChange gives us **confirmed occupancy** pushes — we know the credential was actually accepted by the lock hardware.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Now let me implement. The changes:

1. **Rename `_on_lock_operation` → `_on_node_event`** — dispatch to separate handlers for event IDs 2 and 4
2. **Add `_on_lock_user_change` handler** — filters for PIN (LockDataType=6), pushes UNKNOWN/EMPTY to coordinator
3. **Add optimistic push in `async_set_usercode`/`async_clear_usercode`** — same pattern as Z-Wave
4. **Update docstring** for `_subscribe_to_events` — it now handles both event types
5. **Update README** — "Push Updates: Yes" with note
