  "old_string": "    @callback\n    def _on_lock_operation(self, _event: Any, node_event: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Handle Matter LockOperation events.\n\n        Fires a code slot event when a PIN credential is used to lock/unlock.\n        Only PIN credentials (credentialType=1) trigger the event — other\n        credential types (RFID, fingerprint, etc.) are ignored.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Filter to DoorLock cluster LockOperation events\n        if (\n            getattr(node_event, \"cluster_id\", None) != _DOOR_LOCK_CLUSTER_ID\n            or getattr(node_event, \"event_id\", None) != _LOCK_OPERATION_EVENT_ID\n        ):\n            return\n\n        data: dict[str, Any] = getattr(node_event, \"data\", None) or {}\n        credentials = data.get(\"credentials\")\n        lock_operation_type = data.get(\"lockOperationType\")\n\n        # Must have credentials with a PIN type to fire\n        if not credentials:\n            return\n\n        # Find the PIN credential index (credentialType 1 = PIN)\n        code_slot: int | None = None\n        for cred in credentials:\n            if isinstance(cred, dict) and cred.get(\"credentialType\") == 1:\n                code_slot = cred.get(\"credentialIndex\")\n                break\n\n        # Only fire for PIN credentials\n        if code_slot is None:\n            return\n\n        # Determine lock/unlock from operation type\n        # 0 = Lock, 1 = Unlock, 2 = NonAccessUserEvent, 3 = ForcedUserEvent, 4 = Unlatch\n        if lock_operation_type == 0:\n            to_locked = True\n        elif lock_operation_type == 1:\n            to_locked = False\n        else:\n            to_locked = None\n\n        LOGGER.debug(\n            \"Lock %s: LockOperation event — slot=%s, locked=%s\",\n            self.lock.entity_id,\n            code_slot,\n            to_locked,\n        )\n\n        self.async_fire_code_slot_event(\n            code_slot=code_slot,\n            to_locked=to_locked,\n            action_text=\"locked\"\n            if to_locked\n            else \"unlocked\"\n            if to_locked is False\n            else \"operated\",\n            source_data=data,\n        )",
  "new_string": "    @callback\n    def _on_node_event(self, _event: Any, node_event: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Dispatch DoorLock cluster events to the appropriate handler.\"\"\"\n        if getattr(node_event, \"cluster_id\", None) != _DOOR_LOCK_CLUSTER_ID:\n            return\n\n        event_id = getattr(node_event, \"event_id\", None)\n        if event_id == _LOCK_OPERATION_EVENT_ID:\n            self._handle_lock_operation(node_event)\n        elif event_id == _LOCK_USER_CHANGE_EVENT_ID:\n            self._handle_lock_user_change(node_event)\n\n    @callback\n    def _handle_lock_operation(self, node_event: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Handle LockOperation events (event ID 2).\n\n        Fires a code slot event when a PIN credential is used to lock/unlock.\n        Only PIN credentials (credentialType=1) trigger the event — other\n        credential types (RFID, fingerprint, etc.) are ignored.\n        \"\"\"\n        data: dict[str, Any] = getattr(node_event, \"data\", None) or {}\n        credentials = data.get(\"credentials\")\n        lock_operation_type = data.get(\"lockOperationType\")\n\n        # Must have credentials with a PIN type to fire\n        if not credentials:\n            return\n\n        # Find the PIN credential index (credentialType 1 = PIN)\n        code_slot: int | None = None\n        for cred in credentials:\n            if isinstance(cred, dict) and cred.get(\"credentialType\") == 1:\n                code_slot = cred.get(\"credentialIndex\")\n                break\n\n        # Only fire for PIN credentials\n        if code_slot is None:\n            return\n\n        # Determine lock/unlock from operation type\n        # 0 = Lock, 1 = Unlock, 2 = NonAccessUserEvent, 3 = ForcedUserEvent, 4 = Unlatch\n        if lock_operation_type == 0:\n            to_locked = True\n        elif lock_operation_type == 1:\n            to_locked = False\n        else:\n            to_locked = None\n\n        LOGGER.debug(\n            \"Lock %s: LockOperation event — slot=%s, locked=%s\",\n            self.lock.entity_id,\n            code_slot,\n            to_locked,\n        )\n\n        self.async_fire_code_slot_event(\n            code_slot=code_slot,\n            to_locked=to_locked,\n            action_text=\"locked\"\n            if to_locked\n            else \"unlocked\"\n            if to_locked is False\n            else \"operated\",\n            source_data=data,\n        )\n\n    @callback\n    def _handle_lock_user_change(self, node_event: Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Handle LockUserChange events (event ID 4).\n\n        Pushes occupancy updates to the coordinator when a PIN credential is\n        added, modified, or cleared. This provides real-time change detection\n        without waiting for the next poll cycle.\n\n        Only PIN credentials (LockDataType=6) are handled. The DataIndex field\n        maps to the credential index (code slot number).\n        \"\"\"\n        data: dict[str, Any] = getattr(node_event, \"data\", None) or {}\n\n        # Only handle PIN credential changes (LockDataType 6 = PIN)\n        if data.get(\"lockDataType\") != _LOCK_DATA_TYPE_PIN:\n            return\n\n        code_slot = data.get(\"dataIndex\")\n        if code_slot is None:\n            return\n        code_slot = int(code_slot)\n\n        operation = data.get(\"dataOperationType\")\n\n        if operation == _DATA_OP_CLEAR:\n            resolved: str | SlotCode = SlotCode.EMPTY\n        elif operation in (_DATA_OP_ADD, _DATA_OP_MODIFY):\n            resolved = SlotCode.UNKNOWN\n        else:\n            LOGGER.debug(\n                \"Lock %s: LockUserChange event with unknown operation %s for slot %s\",\n                self.lock.entity_id,\n                operation,\n                code_slot,\n            )\n            return\n\n        LOGGER.debug(\n            \"Lock %s: LockUserChange event — slot=%s, operation=%s, resolved=%s\",\n            self.lock.entity_id,\n            code_slot,\n            operation,\n            resolved,\n        )\n\n        if self.coordinator:\n            self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: resolved})"
}

     1→# Matter Integration
     2→
     3→Lock Code Manager supports Matter locks that have the User Management (USR) feature with PIN credential support via the [Matter](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/matter/) integration.
     4→
     5→## How It Works
     6→
     7→Matter lock PINs are **write-only** — the lock accepts PIN codes but never reveals them back. This means:
     8→
     9→- LCM can set and clear PINs on the lock
    10→- The lock reports whether a credential slot is occupied, but not the actual PIN value
    11→- The code sensor shows the configured PIN (from LCM config) rather than the on-lock value
    12→- On Home Assistant restart, LCM re-sets all configured PINs to guarantee correctness
    13→
    14→## Requirements
    15→
    16→- Home Assistant 2026.4.0 or later
    17→- A Matter lock with User Management (USR) feature and PIN credential support
    18→- The Matter integration configured and connected in Home Assistant
    19→
    20→## Supported Operations
    21→
    22→| Operation | Supported | Notes |
    23→|-----------|-----------|-------|
    24→| Set PIN | Yes | Via `matter.set_lock_credential` service |
    25→| Clear PIN | Yes | Via `matter.clear_lock_credential` service |
    26→| Read PIN | No | Matter spec does not allow reading back PINs |
    27→| Push updates | No | Polling every 5 minutes |
    28→| Code slot events | Yes | Via DoorLock LockOperation events (keypad PIN usage) |
    29→
    30→## Limitations
    31→
    32→- **PINs are write-only**: LCM cannot verify the actual PIN on the lock. The sync indicator assumes the PIN is correct after a successful set.
    33→- **No push updates for code changes**: Changes made at the lock keypad are not detected until the next poll (every 5 minutes). However, lock/unlock events via keypad ARE detected in real time.
    34→- **Restart behavior**: On HA restart, all configured PINs are re-set to the lock. This is a one-time operation per restart and ensures the lock has the correct PINs.
    35→- **PIN changes while masked**: When you change a configured PIN, LCM detects the change and re-sets the new PIN, even though it can't read the old one back.
    36→
    37→## Code Slot Events
    38→
    39→Matter locks report `LockOperation` events when a PIN is used to lock or unlock. LCM subscribes to these events and fires `pin_used` events for automations. This enables the **Slot Usage Limiter** blueprint for Matter locks.
    40→
    41→Note: only PIN credential usage fires events. Other credential types (RFID, fingerprint, etc.) are not currently tracked.
    42→
    43→## Verified Locks
    44→
    45→Matter lock support is new. If you have tested LCM with a specific Matter lock, please open an issue or PR to add it to this list.
    46→
    47→## Troubleshooting
    48→
    49→### Lock not detected
    50→
    51→Ensure the Matter integration is loaded and the lock entity appears in Home Assistant. LCM detects Matter locks by their entity domain (`lock.*` from the `matter` integration).
    52→
    53→### "Does not support user management" error
    54→
    55→The lock's Matter DoorLock cluster does not have the USR (User Management) feature enabled. This is a hardware/firmware limitation.
    56→
    57→### "Does not support PIN credentials" error
    58→
    59→The lock supports user management but not PIN credentials (it may only support RFID or biometric credentials).
    60→
```

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The `supports_push` issue is subtle. In `BaseLock.async_internal_set_usercode` (line 775), after the set call returns, it does `if changed and self.coordinator and not self.supports_push: await self.coordinator.async_request_refresh()`. So with `supports_push=False`, the coordinator refresh will re-read from the Matter service, overwriting our optimistic push. The fix is to set `supports_push=True` — but that triggers `setup_push_subscription`/`teardown_push_subscription` which we handle separately. OR we override the behavior by not using the optimistic pushes in set/clear (let LockUserChange events handle it).
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Let me re-read the push subscription lifecycle to understand the implications of `supports_push = True`.

> AGENT

Now I understand the full picture. If we set `supports_push = True`:
1. `subscribe_push_updates()` calls `setup_push_subscription()` — which we'd need to implement (or it calls the base class which raises)
2. `async_internal_set_usercode` / `async_internal_clear_usercode` skip the `async_request_refresh()` call
3. `unsubscribe_push_updates()` calls `teardown_push_subscription()` on unload

The cleanest approach: set `supports_push = True` and implement `setup_push_subscription` / `teardown_push_subscription` to delegate to our existing `_subscribe_to_events` / unsubscribe logic. This way the optimistic pushes won't be overwritten.

   381→    def subscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:
   382→        """Subscribe to push-based value updates with automatic retry.
   383→
   384→        Calls the provider's setup_push_subscription(). Any exception other than
   385→        ProviderNotImplementedError is treated as a potentially transient failure:
   386→        it is logged at debug level and a one-shot retry is scheduled. Permanent
   387→        errors (ProviderNotImplementedError) propagate immediately.
   388→        """
   389→        # Block retry-driven calls after unsubscribe to prevent in-flight retries
   390→        # from resubscribing after teardown. Explicit calls (from setup or state
   391→        # listener) clear the flag and cancel any stale pending retry.
   392→        if self._push_disabled:
   393→            if self._push_retry and self._push_retry.active:
   394→                return
   395→            self._push_disabled = False
   396→            if self._push_retry:

   398→        try:

   400→        except ProviderNotImplementedError:

   405→                self.lock.entity_id,
   406→                err,
   407→            )
   408→            self._ensure_push_retry().schedule()
   409→        else:

   421→        Implementations MUST be idempotent (no-op if already subscribed).

   249→            return
   250→
   251→        # Find the PIN credential index (credentialType 1 = PIN)
   252→        code_slot: int | None = None
   253→        for cred in credentials:
   254→            if isinstance(cred, dict) and cred.get("credentialType") == 1:
   255→                code_slot = cred.get("credentialIndex")
   256→                break
   257→
   258→        # Only fire for PIN credentials
   259→        if code_slot is None:
   260→            return
   261→
   262→        # Determine lock/unlock from operation type
   263→        # 0 = Lock, 1 = Unlock, 2 = NonAccessUserEvent, 3 = ForcedUserEvent, 4 = Unlatch
   264→        if lock_operation_type == 0:
   265→            to_locked = True
   266→        elif lock_operation_type == 1:
   267→            to_locked = False
   268→        else:
   269→            to_locked = None
   270→
   271→        LOGGER.debug(
   272→            "Lock %s: LockOperation event — slot=%s, locked=%s",
   273→            self.lock.entity_id,
   274→            code_slot,
   275→            to_locked,
   276→        )
   277→
   278→        self.async_fire_code_slot_event(
   279→            code_slot=code_slot,
   280→            to_locked=to_locked,
   281→            action_text="locked"
   282→            if to_locked
   283→            else "unlocked"
   284→            if to_locked is False
   285→            else "operated",
   286→            source_data=data,
   287→        )
   288→
   289→    @callback
   290→    def _handle_lock_user_change(self, node_event: Any) -> None:
   291→        """Handle LockUserChange events (event ID 4).
   292→
   293→        Pushes occupancy updates to the coordinator when a PIN credential is
   294→        added, modified, or cleared. This provides real-time change detection
   295→        without waiting for the next poll cycle.
   296→
   297→        Only PIN credentials (LockDataType=6) are handled. The DataIndex field
   298→        maps to the credential index (code slot number).
   299→        """
   300→        data: dict[str, Any] = getattr(node_event, "data", None) or {}
   301→
   302→        # Only handle PIN credential changes (LockDataType 6 = PIN)
   303→        if data.get("lockDataType") != _LOCK_DATA_TYPE_PIN:
   304→            return
   305→
   306→        code_slot = data.get("dataIndex")
   307→        if code_slot is None:
   308→            return
   309→        code_slot = int(code_slot)
   310→
   311→        operation = data.get("dataOperationType")
   312→
   313→        if operation == _DATA_OP_CLEAR:
   314→            resolved: str | SlotCode = SlotCode.EMPTY
   315→        elif operation in (_DATA_OP_ADD, _DATA_OP_MODIFY):
   316→            resolved = SlotCode.UNKNOWN
   317→        else:
   318→            LOGGER.debug(
   319→                "Lock %s: LockUserChange event with unknown operation %s for slot %s",
   320→                self.lock.entity_id,
   321→                operation,
   322→                code_slot,
   323→            )
   324→            return
   325→
   326→        LOGGER.debug(
   327→            "Lock %s: LockUserChange event — slot=%s, operation=%s, resolved=%s",
   328→            self.lock.entity_id,
   329→            code_slot,
   330→            operation,
   331→            resolved,
   332→        )
   333→
   334→        if self.coordinator:
   335→            self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: resolved})
   336→
   337→    # -- Usercode CRUD -------------------------------------------------------
   338→
   339→    async def async_get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, str | SlotCode]:
   340→        """Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes.
   341→
   342→        Matter PINs are write-only, so occupied slots return SlotCode.UNKNOWN.
   343→        """
   344→        code_slots = {
   345→            int(code_slot)
   346→            for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
   347→            for code_slot in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})
   348→            if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
   349→        }
   350→        if not code_slots:
   351→            return {}
   352→
   353→        lock_data = await self._async_call_service(
   354→            "get_lock_users",
   355→            {"entity_id": self.lock.entity_id},
   356→        )
   357→        users = lock_data.get("users")
   358→        if not isinstance(users, list):
   359→            raise LockCodeManagerError(
   360→                f"Matter get_lock_users response for {self.lock.entity_id} "
   361→                f"has unexpected 'users' value: {users!r}"
   362→            )
   363→
   364→        # Build a set of credential indices that have PIN credentials
   365→        occupied_slots: set[int] = set()
   366→        for user in users:
   367→            for credential in user.get("credentials", []):
   368→                if credential.get("credential_type") != "pin":
   369→                    continue
   370→                cred_index = credential.get("credential_index")
   371→                if cred_index is None:
   372→                    continue
   373→                occupied_slots.add(int(cred_index))
   374→
   375→        LOGGER.debug(
   376→            "Lock %s: %s managed slots, %s occupied",
   377→            self.lock.entity_id,
   378→            len(code_slots),
   379→            len(occupied_slots & code_slots),
   380→        )
   381→        return {
   382→            slot: SlotCode.UNKNOWN if slot in occupied_slots else SlotCode.EMPTY
   383→            for slot in code_slots
   384→        }
   385→
   386→    async def async_set_usercode(
   387→        self, code_slot: int, usercode: str, name: str | None = None
   388→    ) -> bool:
   389→        """Set a usercode on a code slot.
   390→
   391→        Returns True unconditionally because Matter does not reveal whether
   392→        the credential value actually changed. Pushes SlotCode.UNKNOWN to the
   393→        coordinator immediately — the LockUserChange event will confirm.
   394→        """
   395→        await self._async_call_service(
   396→            "set_lock_credential",
   397→            {
   398→                "entity_id": self.lock.entity_id,
   399→                "credential_type": "pin",
   400→                "credential_data": usercode,
   401→                "credential_index": code_slot,
   402→            },
   403→        )
   404→        if name is not None:
   405→            try:
   406→                await self._async_call_service(
   407→                    "set_lock_user",
   408→                    {
   409→                        "entity_id": self.lock.entity_id,
   410→                        "credential_index": code_slot,
   411→                        "user_name": name,
   412→                    },
   413→                )
   414→            except (LockDisconnected, LockCodeManagerError):
   415→                LOGGER.warning(
   416→                    "Lock %s: credential set on slot %s but failed to set "
   417→                    "user name '%s'",
   418→                    self.lock.entity_id,
   419→                    code_slot,
   420→                    name,
   421→                )
   422→        # Optimistic update: service call succeeded, push occupancy state
   423→        # immediately. The LockUserChange event will confirm later.
   424→        if self.coordinator:
   425→            self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: SlotCode.UNKNOWN})
   426→        return True
   427→
   428→    async def async_clear_usercode(self, code_slot: int) -> bool:
   429→        """Clear a usercode on a code slot.
   430→
   431→        Returns True if a credential was cleared, False if the slot was already
   432→        empty. Pushes SlotCode.EMPTY to the coordinator immediately on success.
   433→        """
   434→        lock_data = await self._async_call_service(
   435→            "get_lock_credential_status",
   436→            {
   437→                "entity_id": self.lock.entity_id,
   438→                "credential_type": "pin",
   439→                "credential_index": code_slot,
   440→            },
   441→        )
   442→        if not lock_data.get("credential_exists"):
   443→            return False
   444→
   445→        await self._async_call_service(
   446→            "clear_lock_credential",
   447→            {
   448→                "entity_id": self.lock.entity_id,
   449→                "credential_type": "pin",
   450→                "credential_index": code_slot,
   451→            },
   452→        )
   453→        # Optimistic update: clear succeeded, push empty state immediately.
   454→        # The LockUserChange event will confirm later.
   455→        if self.coordinator:
   456→            self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: SlotCode.EMPTY})
   457→        return True
   458→
   459→    async def async_hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, str | SlotCode]:
   460→        """Perform hard refresh and return all codes.
   461→
   462→        Matter has no cache to invalidate, so this is identical to async_get_usercodes.
   463→        """
   464→        return await self.async_get_usercodes()
   465→

Does not use the push subscription framework\n        because that would disable polling — Matter needs polling for full\n        reconciliation and events for real-time change detection.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._event_unsub is not None:\n            return\n\n        client = self._get_matter_client()\n        node_id = self._matter_node_id\n        if not client or node_id is None:\n            LOGGER.debug(\n                \"Lock %s: Matter client or node ID unavailable, \"\n                \"skipping event subscription\",\n                self.lock.entity_id,\n            )\n            return\n\n        self._event_unsub = client.subscribe_events(\n            callback=self._on_node_event,\n            event_filter=EventType.NODE_EVENT,\n            node_filter=node_id,\n        )\n        LOGGER.debug(\n            \"Lock %s: subscribed to Matter events (node %s)\",\n            self.lock.entity_id,\n            node_id,\n        )\n\n    async def async_unload(self, remove_permanently: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Unload lock and unsubscribe from events.\"\"\"\n        if self._event_unsub:\n            self._event_unsub()\n            self._event_unsub = None\n        await super().async_unload(remove_permanently)",

All 3 review comments on PR #986 addressed:

1. **`dataIndex` int cast** — Added `try/except (TypeError, ValueError)` guard around `int(raw_index)`
2. **Optimistic push overwritten by refresh** — Set `supports_push = True` so `BaseLock.async_internal_set/clear_usercode` skips the post-operation `coordinator.async_request_refresh()` call
3. **Same concern for clear** — Same fix via `supports_push = True`

The key architectural change: Matter now properly uses the push framework (`setup_push_subscription` / `teardown_push_subscription`) instead of manual event subscription. This gives it automatic retry on failure, proper lifecycle management tied to config entry state changes, and correct interaction with the optimistic push updates.

---

## Test Coverage Analysis for PR #986 (feat/matter-push-updates)

### 1. Summary

The test suite is strong at 97% coverage with 56 tests. The new functionality -- LockUserChange event handling, optimistic push updates, and push framework lifecycle -- is well covered with clear, behavior-focused tests. The tests follow good patterns: each test verifies one specific behavior, naming is descriptive, and the happy/sad paths are both represented. There are a few gaps worth noting, mostly in the "important" category rather than "critical."

### 2. Critical Gaps

None. The core behaviors are all tested.

### 3. Important Improvements

**3a. Missing `supports_push` property test -- Criticality: 6/10**

File: `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/tests/providers/test_matter.py`

There are property tests for `domain`, `supports_code_slot_events`, and `usercode_scan_interval` (lines 121-133), but no test for the new `supports_push` property. This property drives whether the push framework is activated at all in `BaseLock`. If someone accidentally changes it to `False`, push updates would silently stop working. Given the other properties are all tested, this is a clear omission.

Suggested test:
```python
async def test_supports_push(matter_lock: MatterLock) -> None:
    """Test that Matter locks support push-based updates."""
    assert matter_lock.supports_push is True
```

**3b. `_on_node_event` with unrecognized DoorLock event ID silently drops -- Criticality: 5/10**

File: `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py`, lines 231-235

When `_on_node_event` receives a DoorLock cluster event with an event ID that is neither 2 (LockOperation) nor 4 (LockUserChange) -- for example event ID 3 (LockOperationError) -- it silently returns. The existing `test_wrong_event_id_ignored` test at line 586 sends `event_id=3` but only checks that `async_fire_code_slot_event` is not called. It does not verify that `push_update` is also not called. If someone adds a handler for event ID 3 that accidentally calls `push_update`, this test would not catch it.

Suggested enhancement: attach a mock coordinator and verify `push_update` is not called for unrecognized DoorLock event IDs.

**3c. `async_set_usercode` does not push when service call raises -- Criticality: 7/10**

File: `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py`, lines 400-431

If `_async_call_service("set_lock_credential", ...)` raises `LockDisconnected`, the method propagates the exception and the optimistic `push_update` on line 430 is never reached. This is correct behavior, but there is no test verifying that `push_update` is NOT called when the service call fails. If someone refactors to catch the exception and continue (or moves the push_update before the service call), the absence of this test means the regression would go undetected.

Suggested test: mock the service to raise `LockDisconnected`, verify the exception propagates AND `mock_coordinator.push_update` is not called.

**3d. `async_clear_usercode` does not push when clear service call raises -- Criticality: 6/10**

Same pattern as 3c but for the clear path. If `clear_lock_credential` raises after `get_lock_credential_status` returns `credential_exists=True`, the push should not happen. No test covers this.

**3e. `_handle_lock_user_change` with non-integer `dataIndex` -- Criticality: 5/10**

File: `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py`, lines 311-313

The code handles `TypeError`/`ValueError` from `int(raw_index)`, but there is no test that exercises this path (e.g., `dataIndex: "abc"`). The `test_missing_data_index_ignored` test only covers `dataIndex` being absent. A malformed dataIndex from a buggy firmware could trigger this path.

### 4. Test Quality Issues

**4a. Direct access to private methods in tests -- Minor concern**

Tests call `matter_lock._on_node_event(...)` directly rather than going through the subscription mechanism. This is acceptable for unit testing the dispatch logic in isolation, and the subscription setup is separately tested in `TestEventSubscription`. No action needed, but worth noting that if the internal method name changes, many tests break. The tests are coupled to the internal API surface rather than the public contract.

**4b. `mock_coordinator.data` is set but never read -- Minor concern**

In tests like `test_pin_added_pushes_unknown` (line 820), `mock_coordinator.data` is set to `{3: SlotCode.EMPTY}` but nothing in the tested code reads `coordinator.data`. This setup is harmless but misleading -- it suggests the test is verifying a state transition when it is only verifying that `push_update` is called with the right arguments. Removing the `.data` assignment would make the intent clearer.

### 5. Positive Observations

- **Comprehensive LockUserChange coverage**: All three operation types (Add, Modify, Clear) are tested with correct SlotCode assertions. Non-PIN data types and missing fields are properly covered.
- **Optimistic push tests are well-structured**: Both `async_set_usercode` and `async_clear_usercode` verify the push call with specific arguments, and the "empty slot returns False with no push" case is covered.
- **Push lifecycle tests are solid**: Idempotent setup, teardown cleanup, error cases (no client, no node ID) all raise `LockDisconnected` as expected.
- **Refactored dispatch is cleanly tested**: The `_on_node_event` dispatcher correctly routes to the two handlers, and wrong-cluster and wrong-event-ID filters are both covered.
- **Good use of shared test mixins**: Connection and availability tests reuse `ServiceProviderConnectionTests` and `ServiceProviderDeviceAvailabilityTests`, avoiding duplication.

### Priority Summary

| Gap | Criticality | Effort |
|-----|------------|--------|
| `supports_push` property test | 6 | Trivial |
| Service failure prevents optimistic push (set) | 7 | Low |
| Service failure prevents optimistic push (clear) | 6 | Low |
| Non-integer `dataIndex` edge case | 5 | Trivial |
| Unrecognized event ID also does not push | 5 | Trivial |

The most impactful addition would be tests 3c and 3a -- verifying that optimistic pushes do not fire on service failures, and that the `supports_push` property is explicitly asserted. These protect the most consequential behavioral contracts introduced in this PR.

- `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/tests/providers/test_matter.py`
- `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/README.md`

## Summary

The PR correctly migrates Matter's event subscription from a manual approach (calling `_subscribe_to_events()` in `setup()` and overriding `async_unload()`) to the BaseLock push framework (`setup_push_subscription` / `teardown_push_subscription`). It adds LockUserChange event handling and optimistic push updates in set/clear methods. The implementation aligns well with the framework contracts defined in `_base.py`.

**No high-confidence issues found (confidence >= 80).**

## Verification Details

1. **Push framework integration**: `supports_push` returns `True`, `setup_push_subscription` and `teardown_push_subscription` are implemented as `@callback` methods, matching the base class contract. The old `async_unload` override was correctly removed -- the base class `async_unload` calls `unsubscribe_push_updates()` which calls `teardown_push_subscription()`. The old manual `_subscribe_to_events()` call in `setup()` was correctly removed -- `BaseLock._async_initialize_lock` calls `subscribe_push_updates()` when `supports_push` is True.

2. **Error handling in setup_push_subscription**: Raises `LockDisconnected` when client/node is unavailable. The base `subscribe_push_updates()` catches all non-`ProviderNotImplementedError` exceptions and schedules a retry, so `LockDisconnected` correctly triggers automatic retry.

3. **Event dispatch**: `_on_node_event` correctly filters by cluster ID first, then dispatches by event ID to separate handlers. This is a clean separation from the previous single-handler approach.

4. **LockUserChange handler**: Correctly filters to PIN credentials only (`lockDataType=6`), handles Add/Modify/Clear operations with appropriate SlotCode values, and gracefully handles missing `dataIndex`, unknown operations, and absent coordinator.

5. **Optimistic push updates**: Both `async_set_usercode` and `async_clear_usercode` push to the coordinator after the service call succeeds but before returning. This matches the pattern documented in AGENTS.md. The `async_clear_usercode` correctly only pushes on actual clears (when `credential_exists` is True), not on already-empty slots.

6. **Idempotency**: `setup_push_subscription` checks `_event_unsub is not None` and returns early, satisfying the base class's idempotency requirement.

7. **Test coverage**: 56 tests pass. New tests cover all LockUserChange scenarios (add/modify/clear, non-PIN ignored, missing dataIndex, unknown operation, no coordinator, wrong cluster) and all optimistic update paths (set pushes UNKNOWN, clear pushes EMPTY, clear on empty slot does not push, no coordinator does not crash). Existing LockOperation tests were updated to use `_on_node_event` instead of the old `_on_lock_operation`.

8. **Project conventions**: Imports use canonical modules. Tests don't manipulate `hass.data` directly for setup (they use the existing fixture pattern). No inline imports. README update is minimal and accurate.

The code is clean, well-documented, and properly integrated with the existing push framework.

## Error Handling Audit: PR #986 (feat/matter-push-updates)

### Issue 1: Silent return on invalid `dataIndex` in `_handle_lock_user_change`

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py`, lines 308-314

**Severity:** HIGH

**Issue Description:** When `raw_index` is `None` (line 309-310) or when `int(raw_index)` raises `TypeError`/`ValueError` (lines 311-314), the function silently returns with no logging. A `dataIndex` that is present but non-integer (e.g., a string like `"abc"` or a float) indicates either a malformed event from the lock firmware or a breaking change in the Matter SDK. Silently discarding this means the user never learns that their lock is sending corrupt events, and debugging becomes a nightmare.

The `None` case is reasonable since the field is optional per spec, but the `TypeError`/`ValueError` case is a data corruption signal that should be logged.

**Hidden Errors:** A Matter SDK update that changes the `dataIndex` type (e.g., from int to string identifier) would be silently swallowed. Firmware bugs producing garbage data would never be surfaced.

**User Impact:** Users would see their slot occupancy not updating in real time with no indication why. They would have to wait for the next poll cycle, and without any log entry, they would have no way to diagnose the delay.

**Recommendation:** Log at warning level when the `int()` cast fails, since this indicates unexpected data rather than a normal filtering case.

```python
raw_index = data.get("dataIndex")
if raw_index is None:
    return
try:
    code_slot = int(raw_index)
except (TypeError, ValueError):
    LOGGER.warning(
        "Lock %s: LockUserChange event has non-integer dataIndex %r, ignoring",
        self.lock.entity_id,
        raw_index,
    )
    return
```

---

### Issue 2: Silent no-op when `self.coordinator` is None during push

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py`, lines 339-340 (event handler), lines 429-430 (set_usercode), lines 460-461 (clear_usercode)

**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Issue Description:** All three push sites use `if self.coordinator:` to guard the `push_update` call. If the coordinator is `None`, the push is silently skipped. While this is tested (the test `test_no_coordinator_does_not_crash` explicitly verifies this), the absence of any logging means that if a coordinator fails to initialize, every subsequent event and CRUD operation silently loses its push update with zero diagnostic output. The coordinator should never be `None` when these paths execute in production (it is set during `_async_setup_internal` before push subscriptions are established), so this condition being true would indicate a serious lifecycle bug.

**User Impact:** If a lifecycle bug causes the coordinator to be `None`, the user would have a lock that appears to accept commands (set/clear return True) but never updates the UI. All push updates would be silently dropped. The user would have no logs to explain why occupancy is stale.

**Recommendation:** Log at debug level when the coordinator is missing, since this is a defensive guard against a lifecycle condition that should not occur.

```python
if self.coordinator:
    self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: resolved})
else:
    LOGGER.debug(
        "Lock %s: coordinator not available, skipping push update for slot %s",
        self.lock.entity_id,
        code_slot,
    )
```

This applies to all three sites. Alternatively, given that the base class docstring for `set_usercode`/`clear_usercode` explicitly documents using `self.coordinator.push_update()`, you could assert the coordinator is present and let it fail loudly, but the debug log is the minimum acceptable response.

---

### Issue 3: `_on_node_event` silently drops unrecognized DoorLock cluster event IDs

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py`, lines 226-235

**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Issue Description:** The dispatcher checks for event IDs 2 and 4, but any other DoorLock cluster event (e.g., event ID 3 = `LockOperationError`) passes through the `if/elif` chain and is silently discarded. There is no `else` clause and no logging for unrecognized event IDs. While it is acceptable to not handle every event type, completely silent discard of unknown events from the same cluster means that new Matter spec events or error events will be invisible.

Notably, `LockOperationError` (event ID 3) is a real DoorLock cluster event that indicates a failed lock/unlock attempt. Silently dropping this is a missed diagnostic opportunity.

**User Impact:** If a lock sends `LockOperationError` events (someone tried a wrong PIN, or a mechanical jam occurred), this information vanishes without trace. Users relying on this integration for security monitoring would have a blind spot.

**Recommendation:** Add a debug log for unrecognized event IDs from the DoorLock cluster.

```python
event_id = getattr(node_event, "event_id", None)
if event_id == _LOCK_OPERATION_EVENT_ID:
    self._handle_lock_operation(node_event)
elif event_id == _LOCK_USER_CHANGE_EVENT_ID:
    self._handle_lock_user_change(node_event)
else:
    LOGGER.debug(
        "Lock %s: unhandled DoorLock cluster event_id=%s",
        self.lock.entity_id,
        event_id,
    )
```

---

### Issue 4: `_get_matter_client` silently returns None on AttributeError

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py`, lines 99-103

**Severity:** MEDIUM (pre-existing, not new in this PR, but now load-bearing for the push framework)

**Issue Description:** The `try/except (StopIteration, AttributeError): return None` block catches `AttributeError`, which could mask bugs beyond the intended "adapter doesn't have matter_client" scenario. For example, if `matter_data.values()` itself raises `AttributeError` because `matter_data` is unexpectedly not a dict (perhaps the Matter integration changed its data structure), this would be silently swallowed and `setup_push_subscription` would raise `LockDisconnected("Matter client or node ID unavailable")` -- an inaccurate error message hiding the real problem.

This is pre-existing code, but it is now more consequential because `setup_push_subscription` depends on it. Previously it only affected the old `_subscribe_to_events` which logged and returned; now it triggers the retry framework with a misleading error.

**Hidden Errors:** Any `AttributeError` in the Matter data access chain is caught: misspelled attribute names in future refactors, None values where objects are expected, or breaking changes in the Matter integration's data structure.

**Recommendation:** This is a pre-existing concern, but worth flagging. At minimum, log the caught exception at debug level so there is a trace.

---

### Issue 5: Optimistic push and event push can create duplicate/conflicting updates

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py`, lines 427-430 (set_usercode optimistic push) and lines 339-340 (event-driven push)

**Severity:** LOW (not an error handling issue per se, but a correctness concern tied to the push framework)

**Issue Description:** When `async_set_usercode` succeeds, it pushes `SlotCode.UNKNOWN` optimistically (line 430). Then the `LockUserChange` event arrives and `_handle_lock_user_change` pushes `SlotCode.UNKNOWN` again (line 340). The `push_update` method in the coordinator has a `if new_data == self.data: return` guard (coordinator.py line 102), so the duplicate is harmless. This is fine. I am noting this as a positive observation -- the coordinator's deduplication correctly handles the race.

---

### Issue 6: `setup_push_subscription` raising `LockDisconnected` -- retry behavior is correct

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/_base.py`, lines 398-408

**Severity:** N/A (correct behavior, positive finding)

**Issue Description:** The base class `subscribe_push_updates` (line 381) catches all exceptions except `ProviderNotImplementedError`, logs at debug level, and schedules a one-shot retry via `_ensure_push_retry().schedule()`. The Matter provider's `setup_push_subscription` raises `LockDisconnected` (a subclass of `LockCodeManagerError`, not `ProviderNotImplementedError`), so it will be caught by the `except Exception` clause and retried. This is the correct behavior as documented. The test `test_setup_push_no_client_raises` verifies the exception is raised, and the base class integration is sound.

---

### Issue 7: No test coverage for `push_update` raising an exception

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/tests/providers/test_matter.py` (entire TestLockUserChangeEvent and TestOptimisticPushUpdates classes)

**Severity:** HIGH

**Issue Description:** All tests use `MagicMock()` for the coordinator, which means `push_update` never raises. But `push_update` calls `self.async_set_updated_data(new_data)` (coordinator.py line 109), which updates HA's `DataUpdateCoordinator` internals. If `self.data` is `None` (coordinator not yet refreshed), the `{**self.data, **updates}` expression on line 99 will raise `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable`. This is a real scenario -- if a `LockUserChange` event arrives before the coordinator's first refresh completes, the push will crash.

In the event callback path (`_handle_lock_user_change`), this `TypeError` would propagate uncaught into the Matter client's event dispatch, potentially breaking the event subscription for all subsequent events (depending on how the Matter client handles callback exceptions). In the `async_set_usercode`/`async_clear_usercode` paths, the exception would propagate to the caller as an unhandled `TypeError` instead of a meaningful error.

**User Impact:** If a `LockUserChange` event fires before the coordinator finishes its first poll, the entire event subscription could break, and neither LockOperation events (security events) nor future LockUserChange events would be processed. The user would get no code slot events and no push updates until a reconnect cycle.

**Recommendation:** Either:
1. Guard against `self.data is None` in the coordinator's `push_update` method (the root fix), or
2. Guard in the Matter provider before calling `push_update`:
```python
if self.coordinator and self.coordinator.data is not None:
    self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: resolved})
```

And add a test that configures `mock_coordinator.data = None` and verifies the behavior.

---

### Issue 8: `_handle_lock_user_change` missing `dataIndex` logs nothing

**Location:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py`, lines 308-310

**Severity:** LOW

**Issue Description:** When `raw_index` is `None`, the function returns silently. This is the most defensible silent return in the PR because the Matter specification allows `LockUserChange` events where `dataIndex` is not applicable (e.g., user-level changes, not credential-level). However, for PIN-specific events (`lockDataType=6`), a missing `dataIndex` is unusual and could indicate a firmware quirk worth knowing about.

**Recommendation:** This is borderline. A debug log would be nice but not critical, since the filter already narrowed to PIN type and a missing index is plausibly spec-compliant.

> DEVELOPER

so now, slot active goes to on -> in sync goes to off -> sync manager sets pin -> sync manager pushes optimistic update to coordinator -> in sysnc goes on -> event comes in with an unknown code for this slot. What do we do with this event? It doesn't seem like it closes the loop on anything

> AGENT

You're right — for LCM-initiated operations, the LockUserChange event is completely redundant. The loop is already closed:

1. `async_set_usercode` succeeds → optimistic push `UNKNOWN` → in-sync goes on
2. LockUserChange arrives → pushes `UNKNOWN` again → coordinator deduplicates → no-op

The event doesn't confirm anything the optimistic push didn't already handle. We said earlier it could serve as "confirmation the operation worked," but the optimistic push already assumed success based on the service call not raising. The LockUserChange event just agrees.

**Where LockUserChange actually adds value:**

- **External changes** — someone adds/clears a PIN at the keypad (`operationSource=3`) or via another controller. No optimistic push exists for those, so the event is the only way to detect the change immediately instead of waiting 5 minutes.
- **External clears** — someone clears a slot LCM manages. The event pushes `EMPTY`, sync manager detects mismatch, re-sets the PIN within one tick.

So the push framework integration (`supports_push=True`) is really justified by external change detection, not by confirming our own operations. The optimistic pushes in set/clear are what close the loop for LCM-initiated work — the LockUserChange subscription is for detecting changes we *didn't* initiate.

Should I update the comments/docstrings to make this distinction clearer?

> DEVELOPER

wondering if we should do optimistic updartes or rely on the events if the provider supports events

> AGENT

Good question. Two approaches:

**A) Optimistic push (current)**: Push immediately after service call succeeds. Event arrives later, deduplicates, no-op. Fastest possible sync — no gap between service call and coordinator update.

**B) Event-only**: Don't push in set/clear. Wait for LockUserChange event to update coordinator. Slightly slower (event delivery latency) but the event is the lock's actual confirmation that the credential was stored.

The argument for B is stronger:

1. **The event IS the confirmation** — the service call succeeding only means HA sent the command. The LockUserChange event means the lock actually processed it. If the lock silently fails to store the credential, B would correctly not update the coordinator.
2. **Single source of truth** — all coordinator updates come from events, whether LCM-initiated or external. Simpler mental model.
3. **Less code** — remove the push from set/clear, remove the `coordinator.data is not None` guards we just added.
4. **Z-Wave is different** — Z-Wave needs optimistic pushes because the value cache update is asynchronous and can cause sync loops with stale reads. Matter doesn't have this problem since `supports_push=True` already skips the post-operation coordinator refresh.

The only downside is a brief window (milliseconds to seconds) where in-sync might flicker off→on after a set, depending on event delivery timing. But with `supports_push=True` skipping the refresh, there's no stale read to cause a sync loop.

Want me to remove the optimistic pushes and rely purely on events?

Z-Wave may still need\n  optimistic pushes to avoid sync loops with stale cache reads.\n\n## Code Quality"

@@ -24,21 +24,24 @@ Matter lock PINs are **write-only** — the lock accepts PIN codes but never rev
 | Set PIN | Yes | Via `matter.set_lock_credential` service |

 ## Limitations
 
 - **PINs are write-only**: LCM cannot verify the actual PIN on the lock. The sync indicator assumes the PIN is correct after a successful set.
-- **No push updates for code changes**: Changes made at the lock keypad are not detected until the next poll (every 5 minutes). However, lock/unlock events via keypad ARE detected in real time.
+- **Occupancy-only push updates**: LCM detects credential changes (add/clear/modify) in real time via LockUserChange events, but cannot see the actual PIN value. External changes are detected immediately rather than waiting for the next poll.
 - **Restart behavior**: On HA restart, all configured PINs are re-set to the lock. This is a one-time operation per restart and ensures the lock has the correct PINs.
 - **PIN changes while masked**: When you change a configured PIN, LCM detects the change and re-sets the new PIN, even though it can't read the old one back.
 
-## Code Slot Events
+## Event Subscriptions
 
-Matter locks report `LockOperation` events when a PIN is used to lock or unlock. LCM subscribes to these events and fires `pin_used` events for automations. This enables the **Slot Usage Limiter** blueprint for Matter locks.
+LCM subscribes to two DoorLock cluster events:
 
-Note: only PIN credential usage fires events. Other credential types (RFID, fingerprint, etc.) are not currently tracked.
+- **LockOperation** (event ID 2): Fires when a PIN is used to lock or unlock. LCM creates `pin_used` events for automations, enabling the **Slot Usage Limiter** blueprint for Matter locks.
+- **LockUserChange** (event ID 4): Fires when a credential is added, modified, or cleared. LCM pushes occupancy updates to the coordinator immediately, so changes are detected in real time rather than waiting for the next poll.
+
+Note: only PIN credential events are tracked. Other credential types (RFID, fingerprint, etc.) are not currently handled.

Commented on #984. The key issues:

1. **Codes not clearing** — Most critical. The sync manager should call `async_clear_usercode` when a slot goes inactive, which calls `matter.get_lock_credential_status` then `matter.clear_lock_credential`. Need debug logs to see if the calls are being made and whether they succeed.

2. **Event entity unavailable** — On 2.0.1 the event subscription used the manual `_subscribe_to_events` (not the push framework). If `_get_matter_client()` or `_matter_node_id` returned None, subscription was silently skipped. On the just-merged 2.0.2 code (PR #986), `setup_push_subscription` raises `LockDisconnected` which triggers retry — that should help. But the user needs to update first.

3. **No events** — Follows from #2. If subscription didn't establish, no events fire.

We need the user's debug logs to diagnose whether the Matter service calls are reaching the lock at all.

> AGENT

Right. Here's the situation with all three PRs and issue #984:

**PR #982 (drift alerting)** — If clearing fails with an exception, the sync manager retries and eventually hits the circuit breaker, creating a `slot_disabled` repair issue. This gives the user visible feedback. But if the clear "succeeds" silently (no exception), #982 doesn't help — the optimistic push marks it `EMPTY`, in-sync goes on, and nobody notices the lock still has the code.

However, on the next poll cycle (5 min), `async_get_usercodes` would see the slot is still occupied → push `UNKNOWN` → sync manager detects mismatch → tries to clear again → loop. That loop would eventually hit the circuit breaker, which #982 surfaces as a repair issue. So #982 **does** help even for the silent-success case, just with a delay.

**PR #983 (lock reset)** — Directly relevant. If the user's Aqara U200 has codes that LCM can't clear, the lock reset step during setup would detect unmanaged codes and offer to clear or adopt them. This gives the user a path to fix the initial state.

**PR #986 (already merged)** — The LockUserChange subscription would tell us definitively whether clears are working. If we call `clear_lock_credential` and no LockUserChange event arrives, the lock didn't process it. This is exactly the "event as confirmation" value we discussed.

All three PRs together paint a much better debugging and recovery picture for this user's scenario. Should we prioritize merging #982 and #983?

   157→        # Note: some providers (Matter, Virtual) only return slots already
   158→        # configured in a Lock Code Manager config entry, so unmanaged codes
   159→        # on those providers will not be detected here. This reset step is
   160→        # most useful for Z-Wave locks which return all occupied slots.
   161→        unmanaged = {
   162→            slot: code
   163→            for slot, code in usercodes.items()
   164→            if code is not SlotCode.EMPTY
   165→            and find_entry_for_lock_slot(hass, lock_entity_id, slot) is None
   166→        }
   167→        if unmanaged:
   168→            result[lock_entity_id] = unmanaged
   169→            lock_instances[lock_entity_id] = lock_instance
   170→    return result, lock_instances
   171→

> AGENT

There's a new copilot comment (2026-04-04T21:04:24Z). It raises a good point: after HA restart, `_consecutive_failures` is 0, so `_reset_backoff` won't enter the `if self._consecutive_failures > 0` block, meaning a persisted `lock_offline` issue from before the restart would never get deleted even if the lock is now reachable.

The fix: call `async_delete_issue` unconditionally on successful poll, not just inside `_reset_backoff`.

## Proposed change

Two changes to improve drift detection alerting:

### 1. Migrate persistent notifications to repair issues
- `async_disable_slot()` in `util.py` now creates repair issues instead of persistent notifications when slots are disabled
- `switch.py` PIN-required notification switched to repair issues
- `sync.py` callers updated (removed `title` parameter)
- Added `AcknowledgeRepairFlow` in `repairs.py` for slot_disabled and pin_required issues
- Added translation strings for `slot_disabled`, `pin_required`, and `lock_offline` issues
- Cleaned up all `persistent_notification` imports from util.py and switch.py

### 2. Coordinator poll failure alerting
- After 12 consecutive poll failures (`POLL_FAILURE_ALERT_THRESHOLD`), creates a `lock_offline` repair issue (WARNING severity, not fixable)
- Auto-dismisses the issue when the lock recovers
- Issue ID is per-lock: `lock_offline_{lock_entity_id}`

I see — `_in_sync` starts as `None`. The initial load block (line 439) sets `_in_sync` for the first time. If the slot starts in sync, `_in_sync` transitions from `None` to `True`. The `if not self._in_sync:` check at line 555 catches `False`→`True` but not `None`→`True`.

The fix: also delete the issue unconditionally when `_in_sync` transitions to `True` for the first time. Simplest approach — just always call `async_delete_issue` when we set `_in_sync = True`, since it's a no-op if the issue doesn't exist:

> AGENT

New round of copilot comments (21:47). Let me categorize:

**Already fixed** (from previous commits):
- `__init__.py:470` — Repair cleanup gated on `unload_ok` ✅
- `coordinator.py` — Removed `async_delete_issue` from shutdown ✅  
- `sync.py:589` — Initial load issue deletion ✅

**New actionable issues:**
1. **`sync.py:494`** — `slot_disabled_` auto-delete on initial load fires even when slot is *disabled* (active=OFF, code empty = "in sync"). The repair gets cleared before user sees it.
2. **`sync.py:589`** — Same concern: slot can be "in sync" while disabled, clearing the repair prematurely.
3. **`__init__.py:472`** — `lock_offline_` is lock-scoped, not entry-scoped. If same lock is in two entries, unloading one clears the issue for both.
4. **`test_coordinator.py:1045`** — Test description mismatch with PR description.

Items 1 and 2 are the same issue — the `slot_disabled_` repair gets cleared when the slot is disabled but "in sync" (no code desired, no code on lock). This is a valid concern. The fix: only delete the issue when the slot is active (enabled).

Repair issues (`slot_disabled_`, `pin_required_`, `lock_offline_`) could become orphaned or be prematurely deleted. This PR adds proper auto-deletion, exception safety, and user feedback.\n\n### 1. Auto-delete repair issues on recovery\n\n- **`slot_disabled_`**: Deleted when slot comes back in sync AND is enabled (`active=ON`). A disabled slot can be \"in sync\" (no code desired, no code on lock) without the circuit breaker condition being resolved, so we only clear the issue when the user re-enables the slot and it syncs successfully. Also cleared on initial load after restart if slot starts in sync and enabled.\n- **`pin_required_`**: Deleted when switch is successfully turned on (PIN is now set).\n- **`lock_offline_`**: Already deleted on recovery via `_reset_backoff()`. Persists across HA restarts by design (`is_persistent=True`). NOT deleted on coordinator shutdown.\n\n### 2. Clean up repair issues on entry unload\n\n- Delete all `slot_disabled_` and `pin_required_` issues for every slot in the entry (uses `get_entry_data` to handle data→options migration).\n- Delete `lock_offline_` only if no other Lock Code Manager entry still manages the same lock (issue is lock-scoped, not entry-scoped).\n- Cleanup is gated on `unload_ok` — issues are not deleted if the unload fails.\n\n### 3. New copilot review with 3 comments. Let me assess:

1. **`sync.py:338`** — Fallback creates `slot_disabled_` issue but slot may still be enabled. Valid concern but acceptable — the issue tells the user to check manually, and the `finally` resets the tracker so it won't loop. Creating a separate issue type would be overengineering.

2. **`test_coordinator.py:1061`** — Says PR description says shutdown deletes the issue, but the code doesn't. This is stale — the PR description was updated to say shutdown does NOT delete (persists by design). The test is correct as-is.

3. **`tests/test_sync.py:290`** — Suggests asserting the slot was actually disabled. But the whole point is that the service call *failed* — the slot was NOT disabled. The test correctly verifies the fallback behavior (issue created, tracker reset).

All three are either already correct or acceptable design trade-offs. No code changes needed.

**Summary**: Copilot's round 3 comments are informational/suggestions, not bugs. The PR description already explains the shutdown persistence behavior (comment 2 is stale context). Comment 1 is a valid future consideration but the current approach (fallback issue + manual check) is the right call for now. Comment 3 misunderstands the test intent — the test is verifying the *failure* path.

PR 987 is ready to merge.

## Proposed change

Fixes repair issue lifecycle gaps found in #982. Repair issues (`slot_disabled_`, `pin_required_`, `lock_offline_`) could become orphaned or be prematurely deleted. This PR adds proper auto-deletion, exception safety, and user feedback.

### 1. Auto-delete repair issues on recovery

- **`slot_disabled_`**: Deleted when slot comes back in sync AND is enabled (`active=ON`). A disabled slot can be "in sync" (no code desired, no code on lock) without the circuit breaker condition being resolved, so we only clear the issue when the user re-enables the slot and it syncs successfully. Also cleared on initial load after restart if slot starts in sync and enabled.
- **`pin_required_`**: Deleted when switch is successfully turned on (PIN is now set).
- **`lock_offline_`**: Already deleted on recovery via `_reset_backoff()`. Persists across HA restarts by design (`is_persistent=True`). NOT deleted on coordinator shutdown.

### 2. Clean up repair issues on entry unload

- Delete all `slot_disabled_` and `pin_required_` issues for every slot in the entry (uses `get_entry_data` to handle data→options migration).
- Delete `lock_offline_` only if no other Lock Code Manager entry still manages the same lock (issue is lock-scoped, not entry-scoped).
- Cleanup is gated on `unload_ok` — issues are not deleted if the unload fails.

### 3. Exception safety for `_disable_slot`

- Wrapped `async_disable_slot` in try/except/finally so `_reset_sync_tracker()` always runs, preventing the slot from getting stuck in limbo.
- On exception, creates the repair issue directly as a fallback so the user is always notified even if the switch service call failed.

### 4. User feedback for PIN-missing toggle

- `async_turn_on` now raises `HomeAssistantError` when PIN is missing, giving the user immediate UI feedback (toast notification) instead of silently staying off.
- Error message is actionable: "Set a PIN code for slot N before enabling it".

        # most useful for Z-Wave locks which return all occupied slots.

that's something we choose isn't it? At least for matter, we can know which slots have been setup already

> AGENT

You're right. The Matter provider's `async_get_usercodes` currently filters to only configured slots:

```python
code_slots = {
    int(code_slot)
    for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
    for code_slot in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})
    if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
}
```

But `get_lock_users` returns *all* users/credentials on the lock — we just choose to filter them down. For the lock reset step, we'd want the unfiltered view.

The options are:

**A) Add a `get_all_usercodes` method** to BaseLock that returns all slots (not filtered by config). Providers override it. The lock reset step calls this instead of `async_get_usercodes`.

**B) Change `async_get_usercodes` to return all occupied slots** and let callers filter. This would change the coordinator's behavior though — it'd suddenly have data for slots it doesn't manage.

**C) Pass a flag** like `include_unmanaged=True` to `async_get_usercodes`.

A is cleanest — separate method, clear intent, no impact on existing sync flow. But this is a broader change that affects the provider interface. Want me to add it now as part of this PR, or make it a follow-up?

You're right — Z-Wave already returns *all* slots from the cache (line 542 iterates all `slots`, not just `code_slots`). The `code_slots` set is computed but only used for the hard refresh check (lines 530-540), not for filtering the output. So Z-Wave's `async_get_usercodes` already returns unmanaged slots.

Matter and Virtual artificially filter. So option B is actually just making Matter/Virtual consistent with Z-Wave — return all occupied slots, let callers filter. The coordinator already handles extra slots fine (it just stores whatever the provider returns).

  "new_string": "    async def async_get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, str | SlotCode]:\n        \"\"\"Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes.\n\n        Returns all occupied PIN credential slots as SlotCode.UNKNOWN (PINs are\n        write-only) and managed empty slots as SlotCode.EMPTY. Unmanaged\n        occupied slots are also included so callers like the lock reset step\n        can detect codes not managed by Lock Code Manager.\n        \"\"\"\n        managed_slots = {\n            int(code_slot)\n            for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)\n            for code_slot in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})\n            if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])\n        }\n\n        lock_data = await self._async_call_service(\n            \"get_lock_users\",\n            {\"entity_id\": self.lock.entity_id},\n        )\n        users = lock_data.get(\"users\")\n        if not isinstance(users, list):\n            raise LockCodeManagerError(\n                f\"Matter get_lock_users response for {self.lock.entity_id} \"\n                f\"has unexpected 'users' value: {users!r}\"\n            )\n\n        # Build a set of credential indices that have PIN credentials\n        occupied_slots: set[int] = set()\n        for user in users:\n            for credential in user.get(\"credentials\", []):\n                if credential.get(\"credential_type\") != \"pin\":\n                    continue\n                cred_index = credential.get(\"credential_index\")\n                if cred_index is None:\n                    continue\n                occupied_slots.add(int(cred_index))\n\n        # Return all occupied slots (managed or not) plus managed empty slots\n        all_slots = managed_slots | occupied_slots\n        LOGGER.debug(\n            \"Lock %s: %s managed slots, %s occupied, %s total\",\n            self.lock.entity_id,\n            len(managed_slots),\n            len(occupied_slots),\n            len(all_slots),\n        )\n        return {\n            slot: SlotCode.UNKNOWN if slot in occupied_slots else SlotCode.EMPTY\n            for slot in all_slots\n        }"
}

  "new_string": "    async def async_get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, str | SlotCode]:\n        \"\"\"Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes.\n\n        Returns all slots stored in the virtual lock plus managed empty slots.\n        Unmanaged occupied slots are included so callers like the lock reset\n        step can detect codes not managed by Lock Code Manager.\n        \"\"\"\n        managed_slots = {\n            int(code_slot)\n            for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)\n            for code_slot in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})\n            if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])\n        }\n        # Include all slots that have data (managed or not)\n        all_slot_keys = {int(k) for k in self._data}\n        all_slots = managed_slots | all_slot_keys\n        data: dict[int, str | SlotCode] = {}\n        for slot_num in all_slots:\n            slot_key = str(slot_num)\n            if slot_key in self._data:\n                data[slot_num] = str(self._data[slot_key][\"code\"])\n            else:\n                data[slot_num] = SlotCode.EMPTY\n        return data"

  "new_string": "    async def async_get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, str | SlotCode]:\n        \"\"\"Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes.\n\n        Returns all occupied PIN credential slots as SlotCode.UNKNOWN (PINs are\n        write-only) and managed empty slots as SlotCode.EMPTY. Unmanaged\n        occupied slots are included so callers like the lock reset config flow\n        step can detect codes not managed by Lock Code Manager.\n        \"\"\"\n        managed_slots = {\n            int(code_slot)\n            for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)\n            for code_slot in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})\n            if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])\n        }\n\n        lock_data = await self._async_call_service(\n            \"get_lock_users\",\n            {\"entity_id\": self.lock.entity_id},\n        )\n        users = lock_data.get(\"users\")\n        if not isinstance(users, list):\n            raise LockCodeManagerError(\n                f\"Matter get_lock_users response for {self.lock.entity_id} \"\n                f\"has unexpected 'users' value: {users!r}\"\n            )\n\n        # Build a set of credential indices that have PIN credentials\n        occupied_slots: set[int] = set()\n        for user in users:\n            for credential in user.get(\"credentials\", []):\n                if credential.get(\"credential_type\") != \"pin\":\n                    continue\n                cred_index = credential.get(\"credential_index\")\n                if cred_index is None:\n                    continue\n                occupied_slots.add(int(cred_index))\n\n        all_slots = managed_slots | occupied_slots\n        LOGGER.debug(\n            \"Lock %s: %s managed, %s occupied, %s total\",\n            self.lock.entity_id,\n            len(managed_slots),\n            len(occupied_slots),\n            len(all_slots),\n        )\n        return {\n            slot: SlotCode.UNKNOWN if slot in occupied_slots else SlotCode.EMPTY\n            for slot in all_slots\n        }"

> AGENT

This test expects empty dict when no slots configured. Now we also query the lock for all occupied slots, so we need to register the mock service. But the simpler fix: the test is correct that with no configured slots AND no `get_lock_users` service registered, it should return empty. But now we removed the early return. We need to still query the lock — the test needs updating.

Actually, the test calls `async_get_usercodes` with no mock service for `get_lock_users`, which will raise. The old code had `if not code_slots: return {}` which skipped the service call entirely. Now we always call the service. The test needs to either register a mock service or we need to handle the "no managed slots and no occupied slots" case.

The right fix: always query the lock (we need to find unmanaged slots), and if the service isn't available, that's a `LockDisconnected` which propagates. The test should register a mock returning empty users:

  "command": "gh pr create --title \"Return all occupied slots from Matter and Virtual providers\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Proposed change\n\nMake `async_get_usercodes` in the Matter and Virtual providers return all occupied slots, not just those managed by a Lock Code Manager config entry. This matches the existing Z-Wave JS behavior where all slots from the cache are returned regardless of management status.\n\n### Why\n\nThe lock reset config flow step (#983) calls `async_get_usercodes` to detect unmanaged codes on locks. Previously, Matter and Virtual only returned managed slots, making unmanaged code detection impossible on those providers.\n\n### Changes\n\n- **Matter**: Returns all PIN credential slots as `SlotCode.UNKNOWN` plus managed empty slots as `SlotCode.EMPTY`. Removed the early return when no managed slots exist (the lock still needs to be queried for unmanaged codes).\n- **Virtual**: Returns all slots with stored data plus managed empty slots.\n- **Test**: Updated `test_get_usercodes_no_configured_slots` to register a mock service (no longer short-circuits).\n\n### Impact on existing behavior\n\nThe coordinator stores whatever `async_get_usercodes` returns. Extra unmanaged slots in the coordinator data are harmless — the sync manager only processes slots that have corresponding entities, and entities are only created for configured slots.\n\n## Type of change\n\n- [ ] Dependency upgrade\n- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)\n- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)\n- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)\n- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests\n\n## Additional information\n\n- 532 tests pass, all pre-commit hooks pass\n- Prerequisite for #983 (lock reset step) to work on Matter/Virtual locks\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1",

> AGENT

Looking at the duplicate check: line 311 calls `self.is_masked_or_empty(other_usercode)` which returns `True` for `SlotCode.UNKNOWN` and `SlotCode.EMPTY`. For Matter, unmanaged slots are `UNKNOWN` — skipped correctly. For Virtual, unmanaged slots have real PIN values — they WOULD trigger duplicate detection.

This is actually correct behavior for Z-Wave (which already returns all slots). If an unmanaged slot on a Z-Wave lock has the same PIN as a managed slot, duplicate detection fires. The Virtual provider is now consistent with that. The `conflicting_slot_managed=self.is_slot_managed(other_code_slot)` flag tells the downstream handler it's an unmanaged slot.

> AGENT

Yes — line 320 unconditionally overwrites the entire slot config with a fresh dict. If the slot already existed in `self.data[CONF_SLOTS]` (same PIN from another lock), it loses any existing name or other settings. And the conflict check only compares PINs — if PINs match, it still overwrites name/enabled.

But wait — this is a new config entry flow (`async_step_user`). `self.data[CONF_SLOTS]` is empty at this point (it's only populated by adopt itself or the UI/YAML steps that come after). The only way a slot exists here is if a previous lock in the same adopt loop already added it. So the concern is really about the multi-lock same-slot case, not about overwriting pre-existing user config.

That said, the fix is still good practice — use `setdefault` or merge instead of full replace:

> AGENT

Actually, thinking about this more — this is a brand new config entry (the `async_step_user` flow). There's no pre-existing user config to preserve. The only scenario where a slot already exists in `self.data[CONF_SLOTS]` during adopt is if an earlier lock in the same loop already added it (multi-lock, same slot). The `continue` for matching PINs prevents overwriting the first lock's entry.

But your question raises a deeper point: should adopt work during options flow too (adding locks to an existing entry)? In that case, there *would* be existing slot config. That's a future consideration though — right now the lock reset step only runs during initial setup.

> AGENT

Right — in the options flow, existing managed slots would appear in `async_get_usercodes` results, but they're managed by *this* entry. The `_async_get_unmanaged_codes` filter (`find_entry_for_lock_slot` / `managed_slots` check) would correctly exclude them since they're already managed. But if a slot was removed from the entry in the same options update and then the lock reset runs, it would appear as "unmanaged" even though the user just removed it intentionally.

That's the key nuance for the options flow: the lock reset check needs to compare against the *new* slot config (what the user is submitting), not the *current* stored config. Otherwise removing a slot from an entry could trigger "unmanaged code found" for the slot you just removed.

This is captured in the TODO. For now the lock reset only runs in the initial setup flow where there's no pre-existing config to conflict with.

> DEVELOPER

right but also, if I was managing slot 1, and I update to include slot 2, if it's a matter lock, slot 1 will show as unknown. We can reset it if we want to be safe but we should note that's what's happening

> AGENT

Good point. In the options flow with Matter:

1. User manages slot 1 (PIN set, shows UNKNOWN)
2. User adds slot 2 in options
3. Lock reset runs on the updated lock → queries `async_get_usercodes`
4. Slot 1 returns as UNKNOWN — it's managed by this entry, but `managed_slots` is computed from the *current* config which still has slot 1, so it's filtered out ✓
5. Slot 2 (if occupied) shows as unmanaged → offered for adopt/clear ✓

Actually that works. But the tricky case: what if the user *removes* slot 1 from the config in the same update? Then slot 1 is no longer managed → shows as "unmanaged UNKNOWN" → offered for clear. That's actually correct behavior — you're no longer managing it, so offering to clear it makes sense.

The real issue you're raising: if we re-set all managed slots "to be safe" after lock reset, we'd re-set slot 1's PIN even though nothing changed. For Matter that's harmless (write-only, same PIN), but it's unnecessary churn and the user should know it's happening.

This is all options-flow behavior though. Let me make sure the TODO captures these nuances:

Yeah, I agree — the guard clauses with `continue` make this hard to follow. An inner function that raises on skip conditions would read much cleaner:

```python
async def _query_lock(lock_entity_id):
    """Query one lock, raising on skip conditions."""
    lock_entry = ent_reg.async_get(lock_entity_id)
    if not lock_entry:
        raise LockCodeManagerError(f"Entity {lock_entity_id} not found")
    ...
    return lock_instance, unmanaged

for lock_entity_id in lock_entity_ids:
    try:
        lock_instance, unmanaged = await _query_lock(lock_entity_id)
    except LockCodeManagerError:
        continue
```

But we have two different log levels (warning vs debug for unsupported platform). Let me think about whether a custom exception or just a single `except` with the message baked in is cleaner.

Actually simplest: the inner function returns the result or raises, and the outer loop catches with one `except`. The different log levels can be handled inside the inner function before raising.

Much cleaner. The outer loop is now just:

```python
for lock_entity_id in lock_entity_ids:
    try:
        lock_instance, unmanaged = await _query_lock(lock_entity_id)
    except LockCodeManagerError:
        continue
    except Exception:
        _LOGGER.warning(...)
        continue
    if unmanaged:
        result[lock_entity_id] = unmanaged
        lock_instances[lock_entity_id] = lock_instance
```

All the validation/logging lives in `_query_lock` which raises `LockCodeManagerError` for expected skips and lets unexpected exceptions propagate.

Done. `_async_check_existing_usercodes` is now a top-level function with explicit parameters — validates the lock entity, creates a temporary provider instance, queries usercodes, and filters to unmanaged slots. Raises `LockCodeManagerError` for expected skips, lets provider exceptions propagate.

> DEVELOPER

Query locks for usercodes and return only unmanaged ones. Why do we have to prefilter?

> AGENT

You're right — the filtering should happen in `_async_get_unmanaged_codes`, not in `_async_check_existing_usercodes`. The inner function should just query the lock and return everything. The caller decides what's unmanaged.

That makes `_async_check_existing_usercodes` reusable for the options flow too, where the definition of "unmanaged" would be different (based on the new config being submitted).

```

This appears in `async_step_lock_reset_clear` (all slots) and `async_step_lock_reset_adopt` (masked slots only). The only difference is which slots to clear.

A helper method on the flow class:

```python
async def _clear_slots(
    self, slots_to_clear: dict[str, list[int]]
) -> None:
    """Clear specified slots on each lock, logging failures."""
    for lock_entity_id, slots in slots_to_clear.items():
        lock_instance = self._lock_instances.get(lock_entity_id)
        if not lock_instance:
            _LOGGER.warning(
                "No lock instance for %s; cannot clear codes",
                lock_entity_id,
            )
            continue
        for slot in slots:
            try:
                await lock_instance.async_internal_clear_usercode(
                    slot, source="direct"
                )
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                _LOGGER.warning(
                    "Failed to clear slot %s on %s",
                    slot, lock_entity_id, exc_info=True,
                )
```

Then the callers become:

```python
# Clear step: clear all unmanaged slots
await self._clear_slots({
    lock_id: list(codes) for lock_id, codes in self._unmanaged_codes.items()
})

# Adopt step: clear only masked slots
await self._clear_slots({
    lock_id: [s for s, c in codes.items() if c is SlotCode.UNKNOWN]
    for lock_id, codes in self._unmanaged_codes.items()
})
```
